articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Dinamarca vs Portugal
articles.standfirst: Versus te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Dinamarca y Portugal en el Parken de Copenhague correspondiente a la tercera jornada del Grupo A4 de la UEFA Nations League
articles.summary: Versus te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Dinamarca y Portugal en el Parken de Copenhague correspondiente a la tercera jornada del Grupo A4 de la UEFA Nations League
articles.body: Dinamarca recibe a Portugal este jueves en el Parken de Copenhague, en un duelo directo por el liderato del Grupo A4 de la UEFA Nations League. El conjunto danés afronta el encuentro con la oportunidad de alcanzar a los lusos en la primera plaza tras un arranque irregular en este parón de selecciones. Se impuso con solvencia por 2-0 al Gales, pero cayó después por 3-2 ante Noruega, en un partido en el que Erling Haaland firmó un doblete para desnivelar la balanza a favor de los escandinavos. Favorito para el partido entre Dinamarca y Portugal Por su parte, Portugal llega a Copenhague como líder del grupo con puntaje perfecto. El conjunto de Jorge Jesus, que debutó en el banquillo luso con un ajustado 1-0 ante Gales, confirmó su buen momento con una victoria por 2-1 en Oslo ante Noruega. Los vigentes campeones de la competición buscan así prolongar su condición de invictos y sentenciar prácticamente el liderato del grupo antes de la última ventana de noviembre. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito a Portugal, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia dado el buen nivel mostrado por Dinamarca en este parón. Versus paga la victoria lusa a cuota 2.12, por 3.6 del empate y 3.2 de la victoria del cuadro danés. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. Dinamarca ha encajado tres goles en su última salida ante Noruega, mostrando cierta fragilidad defensiva, mientras que Portugal, pese a su condición de líder invicto, tampoco ha logrado mantener su portería a cero en ninguno de sus dos partidos disputados en este parón. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es alta. Versus paga a 1.6 el "sí" y a 2.25 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con bastante producción ofensiva. Entre los dos conjuntos suman ya ocho goles en sus dos primeros partidos de esta Nations League, con Dinamarca sumando cuatro tantos y Portugal tres. Con estos datos, Versus sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 1.73, por 2.1 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. Dinamarca, con un juego intenso y de presión alta característico del combinado escandinavo, suele generar un buen número de saques de esquina jugando en el Parken. Portugal, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus dos últimos partidos un estilo también ofensivo y de banda, apoyado en jugadores como Rafael Leão y Bernardo Silva, lo que invita a pensar en un partido con un reparto ajustado de córners entre ambos combinados. Versus paga a 1.7 que se saquen más de 9 córners, por 2.05 del caso contrario.

articles.title: El Manchester City, favorito al descenso
articles.standfirst: Para Sportium es el tercer candidato a ser relegado de la Premier
articles.summary: Para Sportium es el tercer candidato a ser relegado de la Premier
articles.body: Hace apenas unos meses, la idea habría parecido una broma. Hoy existe la posibilidad. Después de que una comisión independiente lo haya declarado culpable de 114 de los 115 cargos por infringir las normas financieras de la Premier League, el Manchester City se ha colado como tercer favorito para descender en las casas de apuestas, una posibilidad remota que el mercado ya no descarta. El veredicto cierra una de las etapas más largas del fútbol inglés reciente. La Premier formuló las acusaciones en 2023 y la vista ante la comisión arrancó en septiembre de 2024, con doce semanas de audiencias. Sin embargo, el proceso está lejos de terminar. La sanción todavía no se ha determinado, el club mantiene que es inocente y tiene previsto recurrir. El reglamento deja un abanico enorme de castigos posibles, desde una multa ilimitada hasta la deducción de puntos o, en el extremo, la expulsión de la competición. Esa incertidumbre es precisamente lo que alimenta las cuotas. En Sportium, el descenso lo encabeza el Hull, a 1.72, seguido del Ipswich, a 2.10. El City aparece tercero, a 2.62, por delante del Crystal Palace, a 3.50, y del Fulham, a 4.00. Que se sitúe por encima de equipos acostumbrados a sufrir por la permanencia da idea de cómo valora el mercado el riesgo de un castigo severo. Ahora bien, ese riesgo depende por completo de la magnitud de la sanción. Los precedentes recientes en la Premier son de una escala muy inferior. El Nottingham Forest perdió cuatro puntos y el Everton seis, tras una reducción en apelación, por incumplimientos que las comisiones calificaron de menores. El caso del City, en cambio, se refiere a infracciones que se extienden durante casi una década, y algunos expertos, como el analista financiero Kieran Maguire, han hablado de recortes que podrían moverse entre los 60 y los 100 puntos. Es una opinión, no una previsión oficial, pero ayuda a entender por qué el descenso ha dejado de ser un escenario de ciencia ficción. Lo más llamativo es que el mismo mercado de apuestas deportivas que ve al City en la zona de peligro sigue pagando a 1.40 que termine entre los cuatro primeros. Esto tiene una explicación. Las casas dan por factible una sanción de entre 10 y 15 puntos, que dejaría al equipo aún con margen para la Liga de Campeones. Así, el mercado reparte su apuesta entre dos futuros muy distintos, uno de castigo moderado y otro catastrófico, y deja en medio muy poco terreno. La cuota del título en Sportium refuerza esta lectura. Ganar la liga se paga a 4.33, más lejos que antes del veredicto, pero suficiente para mantener al City como segundo favorito. Ni siquiera una condena casi total ha bastado para que las casas den por perdida su temporada, algo que habla tanto de la fortaleza deportiva de la plantilla como de la confianza en que la sanción no será devastadora. Todo dependerá de dos fechas que aún no existen, como son la de la publicación del castigo y la de la resolución de un posible recurso. Cualquier filtración sobre su alcance moverá las cuotas en cuestión de minutos, y no es descartable que instancias superiores acaben modificando lo decidido, como ya ocurrió en su día con la sanción de la UEFA, revocada por el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo. Hasta entonces, el City vive en una situación inédita. Es candidato al título, aspirante a la zona Champions y, a la vez, tercer favorito para bajar. Nunca un mismo club había sido tan favorito y tan vulnerable a la vez.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | After two Asian Games medals, Harita Bhadra sets her sights on 22.45s and World Championships
articles.summary: Before the Asian Games, Harita Bhadra had a fairly modest definition of success. A personal best, she had said, would make her happy.
articles.body: Before the Asian Games, Harita Bhadra had a fairly modest definition of success. A personal best, she had said, would make her happy. A podium finish was what she wanted to chase.She will now leave Aichi-Nagoya with two bronze medals - one from the women’s 200m and another from the mixed 4x100m relay, where she ran the anchor leg as India set a national record of 41.06 seconds.“I’m very happy because I got like two medals at the end of the day. Getting on the podium is like one of the best feelings, especially when you’re representing India, and you’re getting a medal for your country. So that was a very surreal experience for me,” Bhadra told Timesofindia.com from Japan.“And I didn’t get a personal best, but considering the weather conditions and everything, I feel like I gave my best. So that’s okay,” she added.It was also Bhadra’s first senior international competition representing India. She had not been through a junior international programme in Indian colours before arriving in Japan, so much of what she encountered in Aichi-Nagoya was new - the scale of the stadium, the pressure of the races and the closeness of the competition - but she found out quickly that training cannot reproduce all of that.“I’ve definitely learned a lot from this competition and definitely even discovered a lot about myself actually,” she said. “Such scenarios [can be experienced] only in competition, and the level of the pressure and the level of execution will only increase as you go higher and higher.”“But I discovered how strong I can be mentally. If I tell my mind to do something, it can do it.”Before the race, Bhadra knew she belongedWatching Bhadra through the Games, there was a noticeable contrast. Before the races, she was quiet and composed, but her expressions would change once she crossed the line. The happiness was immediate.“On the start line, my only mindset is that I belong over here,” she replied when asked what he goes through between those two moments.“I don’t have to be scared of any of my competitors because, even I’m on the same start line. I just try to trust my body, and I’m not thinking about anything because I’m just staying in the moment, and I’m just trusting my body that all the work I have done is like my body is ready to execute it.”That composure, however, did not mean the nerves had disappeared before her 200m final. Rather, Bhadra says she was nervous. The Reliance Foundation-backed athlete had already given herself a good platform in the heats, finishing second with 23.31s, behind Singapore’s Shanti Pereira.“Everybody on the start line is nervous, but you just accept it. You’re nervous, but that doesn’t mean you’re not confident at the same time. It’s just a mix of both things: you can be nervous but also be equally confident at the same time.”The 200m bronze came down to 0.01 secondsThe finish, though, was nerve-racking - to say the least. Pereira won in 22.78s, with China’s Chen Yujie taking silver in 22.93s. Bhadra crossed in 23.20s, but Japan’s Abigeirufuka Ido was only 0.01 seconds behind in 23.21s. That meant the bronze was decided by the narrowest of margins, with the photo finish separating Bhadra from the Japanese sprinter.For a few seconds after the finish, Bhadra was unsure where she had finished. She had expected the results to appear on the screen opposite the finish line. After the race, she went across to teammate Unnati Aiyappa and sat with her. Unnati eventually pointed towards another screen. “She was like, ‘You have come third’, and that’s when I realised that I have come third.”The medal was secure, but the race itself still had things Bhadra wanted to improve. “You will never be satisfied with a race. There is always something you will feel that, okay, this could have been done better. This part could have been executed better,” she said.For the 23-year-old, more international exposure should help with that. The stage was completely new, and she felt there were sections of the race she could have handled better.“I know I had more left in me, but I trust the process, and I trusted that whenever I know I can, I will execute that race that I have in my mind.”One part of the race, though, had given her evidence that the work was moving in the right direction. The last 30 metres, something which had worked on, with her coach Rohit Mane at Reliance Foundation.“Yes, definitely, because I think I won the race because of the last 30 metres. So that improvement was clearly there.”Bhadra’s coach Mane was not in Japan for the Games, but they stayed in touch through video calls and regular calls, while the relay group had the support of Reliance Foundation’s Martin Owens and James Hillier, along with the AFI coaches, around them in Japan.The coaches, she said, kept reminding the four runners that the work had already been done and that they had to trust the runner alongside them. “They kept us motivated to like trust each other. And that's how we also trusted our partners more.”The relay brought a different kind of pressureBy the time Bhadra returned to the track for the mixed 4x100m relay, she had already raced twice. The stadium was no longer unfamiliar.“I was definitely more confident because I had, like, two races' experience,” she said. “I knew now how it’s going to feel like, on the start, and I knew how I will feel stepping into the stadium and everything, how the call room is.”“I was more calm and settled because I was familiar with the environment, basically. So going into the relay, I felt more collected than I was in 200.”The quartet of Gurindervir Singh, Sneha Shanuvali, Animesh Kujjur and Bhadra had been working on the event well before arriving in Nagoya. The Asian Games camp in Bhubaneswar in August, followed by an acclimatisation camp in Tsukuba.They trained the relay twice a week during the camp. As the Games approached, that came down to once a week because all four athletes also had individual events to prepare for.Bhadra ran the anchor leg in both the semifinal and final, producing strong finishes on each occasion. In the semifinal, she had to recover after a difficult baton exchange on the bend, but still produced the run that carried India into the final. In the medal race, her late surge again proved crucial as India secured bronze. The decision to use Bhadra as the anchor, she says, was made by the coaching staff and AFI team.“They decided to give me the anchor leg. So I was like, okay, I will do the anchor leg. That’s it.”The semifinal did test that decision almost immediately. Kujur fell during the baton exchange before Bhadra took the baton and glanced back for a fleeting second, but with the baton in hand, she focused on the job at hand.“My only thing was I have got the baton. So he [Kujur] has done his job of giving me the baton. So my job is to make the team qualify. As soon as I finished, I was just looking out, like just trying to understand what actually happened. I was trying to see if Animesh is okay or what actually happened.”Studies can wait. The next number is 22.45There was another decision from earlier in the year that Bhadra had wanted to test properly: putting her studies on hold and giving sprinting her full attention.She had not made the decision because she could not handle both. She wanted to find out what would happen if she did not have to divide her time.“I just wanted to give myself the chance to explore how it would be like. I only have to just focus on track and I don’t have to juggle two things at once,” she said.Track, she said, requires time and dedication. “I am very happy with the decision. It was a good decision. I’m happy I gave myself the opportunity to explore how it would be.”Her family being in Japan made the week different too. She had wanted them to see her compete at a major event, and they were there for it.“I actually loved it that my family was there because I was just so excited that they are going to see me run at such a big event, like one of the biggest events of my athletics career so far,” she said.“I was very happy they could be there with me because it just made everything like 100 times more special.”Having ticked one of the big markers for this year, Bhadra is eyeing higher goals now, and her next target is already clear.“I am chasing to qualify for the World Championships in 2027.”The World Championships and eventually the Olympics, which had seemed further away before Aichi-Nagoya, now feel a little closer too. “Yes, definitely. It’s a step closer to, like, step higher, step closer. The qualifying mark is 22.45s for 200 metres.”She believes it is achievable. Bhadra’s personal best in 200m currently stands at 23.14s, which she clocked in June this year.“It is doable. But yeah, it is closer but still a lot of work to do there,” said Bhadra, pausing briefly before answering.The area she wants to work on most is not the one a stopwatch will immediately show. It is the mental side. “On the starting line, before even starting the race, if you are mentally not strong, you have lost the race. Everybody is so close, like I said, 0.01 seconds. Like, it’s like nothing.”Her answer is to stay calm enough to keep competing when the race is still there to be won. “You have to have that mental thing of not giving up, of believing that, ‘No, I can still win.’”She still wants to take it one day at a timeFor Bhadra, being mentally calm and connected to the race is now part of the work alongside the physical preparation. She is not planning to choose between the 100m and 200m just yet.The two events, she says, complement each other. Training for the 100m helps the 200m, and vice versa. She will take an off-season before her coach puts together the next plan.As for a favourite?“I have my days of choosing 100 and some days of choosing 200. I can’t choose for sure.”The medals have not changed the way she wants to approach the next season either. Before the Games, Bhadra had spoken about taking things one day at a time. She still uses the same approach now, even with the attention that will come after two Asian Games medals.“I really don’t think about expectations. Over there, I’m just running for myself. I’m not running for anybody else. The only thing is, yes, every day has to be an improvement, even if it is little. But my only goal is to take it one day at a time and to improve from the previous day,” she said.For now, there is no elaborate celebration planned. Her family is staying in Japan for a few more days to explore the country. Once she returns, Bhadra wants to meet her coach and ‘show off’ the two medals. Then there will be family and friends at home.And then there is Dagina.The handmade jewellery brand Bhadra started in October 2025 will turn one next month. She designs and makes the pieces herself and, because it remains a hobby, handles the work on her own. The Asian Games build-up and the last two months in camp meant she had not been able to spend much time on it.She had started Dagina as a way of taking her mind away from athletics. Now Japan has given her an idea for what comes next.“Now, once I’m back, I’m going to start again, maybe do a collection inspired by Japan or something like that.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: World Grand Prix: Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton to meet in last eight
articles.summary: Former champions Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton have set up an all-Welsh World Grand Prix quarter-final in Leicester on Friday.
articles.body:
Former champions Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton have set up an all-Welsh World Grand Prix quarter-final in Leicester on Friday.

Price gained revenge over England's Ross Smith - who beat the former world champion in the World Series final earlier in September - winning their latest encounter in straight sets.

"It wasn't a brilliant game, but a win's a win and I'm still in the tournament," said Price, who is yet to drop a set in this year's event.

Clayton won his second round match 3-1 against Dutchman Wessel Nijman, averaging 93 and landing eight 180s.

"It felt good up there," said Clayton, who will become the new Welsh number one if he lifts his second World Grand Prix crown on Sunday.

"There's banter between me and Gezzy (Price)", he added.

"Every time Gezzy gets back to [Welsh] number one, he sends me a flag with a number one on.

"We have good banter... [we're] good friends, world number four and five, you can't fault that from Wales."

On Friday's last-eight meeting Price said: "I remember years ago, Jonny in the final of this tournament absolutely smashed me.

"He played pretty decent today, I think he got lucky first round. Hopefully he doesn't get lucky in the next round."

articles.title: Asian Games: Ganesh Mani Ratnam wins bronze as India finish with four compound archery medals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India added another medal to their Asian Games 2026 tally on Thursday as Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru secured bronze in the men’s individual
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India added another medal to their Asian Games 2026 tally on Thursday as Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru secured bronze in the men’s individual compound archery event at Aichi-Nagoya.Ganesh produced a dominant performance in the bronze-medal match, defeating Vietnam’s Cong Duc Dang 149-144. The Indian archer was almost flawless, hitting 10s with 14 of his 15 arrows to comfortably seal the podium finish.The bronze took India’s overall medal tally to 63, comprising 10 gold, 22 silver and 31 bronze.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleGanesh dominates bronze-medal contestGanesh made an ideal start to the bronze-medal match, opening with a perfect 10 while Cong managed an 8. The Vietnamese archer responded with two 10s, but Ganesh matched him with two more perfect shots to maintain his advantage.The Indian completed the opening end with a perfect 30/30, while Cong finished on 29, giving Ganesh a one-point lead.He continued to maintain his accuracy through the remaining ends, with his consistent shooting eventually giving him a five-point winning margin.Ganesh's 149 was enough to comfortably see off Cong, who finished on 144, and secure India's fourth medal in compound archery at the Games.Four compound archery medals for IndiaGanesh's bronze came a day after India enjoyed a hugely successful outing in the compound events, winning three gold medals on Wednesday.His medal also ensured India added another bronze to their growing tally, taking the country's haul to 63 medals.Ganesh had earlier narrowly missed out on a place in the gold-medal contest after losing his semifinal 144-148 to Kim Jongho of South Korea. The Indian began the final end with consecutive 9s, but the deficit proved too difficult to overturn as Kim held on to advance to the final.Ganesh bounced back strongly in the bronze-medal match, delivering a near-perfect performance to finish on the podium.The focus in archery now shifts to the recurve events, which begin on Friday, giving India's archers another opportunity to add to the country's medal tally at Aichi-Nagoya.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: He conducido el CUPRA Raval Endurance: el eléctrico que combina emoción con racionalidad
articles.standfirst: Tras haber probado el CUPRA Raval VZ, ahora lo hacemos con su versión más racional: el Endurance, con el que no echarás de menos dichas siglas y, además, llegarás más lejos
articles.summary: Tras haber probado el CUPRA Raval VZ, ahora lo hacemos con su versión más racional: el Endurance, con el que no echarás de menos dichas siglas y, además, llegarás más lejos
articles.body: Todavía resuenan en mi interior los ecos de la prueba del Raval VZ. La versión más potente y también más ambiciosa dinámicamente hablando del nuevo eléctrico de CUPRA se ha convertido, sin que él lo sepa, en uno de mis referentes, consiguiendo que no eche en falta el disponer de un motor de combustión. Porque, más allá de sus 226 CV, lo que realmente le define es su puesta a punto, la misma que se rodea de elementos como un diferencial autoblocante electrónico, suspensión adaptativa DCC Sport, neumáticos de 235 mm y una puesta a punto pensada para llevar al límite las posibilidades de la nueva plataforma eléctrica de tracción delantera del Grupo Volkswagen. Ahora hemos vuelto a ponernos a sus mandos, pero en una configuración que resulta más lógica para la mayoría de los usuarios: el Endurance. Desarrolla 211 CV, pierde algunos de los elementos específicos del VZ, pero, a cambio, ofrece hasta 446 kilómetros de autonomía (el registro más elevado de toda la gama). Además, cuesta 4.060 euros menos. Sin embargo, ¿sigue siendo tan emocionante de conducir? Después de conducirlo por las carreteras asturianas, te respondemos. Antes de entrar en su comportamiento (que sabemos que es lo que estás buscando), es de recibo mencionar que no hay apenas diferencias estéticas relevantes frente al VZ y, a excepción de montar las llantas Defier de 18 pulgadas en lugar de las Rebel Cooper de 19 (que sí están en opción) o de, precisamente, los detalles en cobre de algunas zonas, el coche es el mismo. Además, opcionalmente, vas a poder elegir la pintura iridiscente, que cambia de tono en función de la incidencia de la luz, aportando mucha más exclusividad al conjunto. Dentro ocurre algo parecido. El salpicadero mantiene la doble pantalla con un cuadro digital de 10,25 pulgadas y un monitor central flotante de 12,9, mientras que los asientos bucket tapizados en Dinamica del VZ dejan paso a unos asientos Sport Pulse que sujetan tan correctamente como los otros, resultando más cómodos para viajar. Pero lo importante es que no pierde ninguno de los elementos que posteriormente emplearemos en la conducción, como el volante deportivo con botones satélite, los diferentes perfiles de conducción, el ESC Sport, el sonido específico que acompaña al acelerador cuando seleccionamos los programas más dinámicos o las levas para regular la recuperación energética. Del mismo modo, mantiene la que es una de sus grandes virtudes, el maletero, el cual puede llegar a los 441 litros en su configuración más amplia, rebajándose en unos 40 litros en el caso de que decidamos incorporar el sistema de sonido Sennheiser. La principal conclusión a la que llegamos tras conducir el Endurance es que no hace falta comprar el VZ para entender el gran trabajo que CUPRA ha realizado con este coche. Si bien todos los Raval parten de la arquitectura MEB+, la misma que el Volkswagen ID. Polo, lo cierto es que la configuración desarrollada por la firma española cambia por completo la percepción del coche. En este caso, no se han limitado a un ajuste nimio, sino que, incluso en esta versión Endurance, el chasis está 15 milímetros más cerca del suelo, las vías son 10 mm más anchas y la suspensión adopta una calibración específica. También cambia la dirección, más rápida y directa que en otros modelos desarrollados sobre la misma familia técnica. La única diferencia frente al VZ es que el Endurance no dispone del diferencial autoblocante e-LSD ni del DCC Sport con 15 niveles de ajuste reservados al VZ, pero, siendo justos, no los necesitamos ni los echamos en falta. Cierto es que el VZ nos dejó encandilados tanto al conducirlo bajo camuflaje como en la primera prueba, pero, en una carretera convencional, sin estar buscando constantemente el límite de adherencia, la diferencia con este Endurance es menor de lo que podríamos esperar al inicio. El coche entra en curva con solvencia, apoya sin movimientos exagerados y permite enlazar cambios de dirección con una facilidad poco habitual entre los eléctricos de este tamaño. La batería continúa aportando masa, evidentemente, y los 1.610 kilos que cifra frente a la báscula le impiden hablar de la ligereza de un utilitario tradicional, pero la colocación del acumulador bajo el piso y un centro de gravedad bajo ayudan a que esa cifra se perciba mucho menos desde nuestro asiento. La suspensión tiene un punto firme, como corresponde al planteamiento de CUPRA, aunque no cae en el error de que percibamos cada irregularidad del asfalto como un golpe seco. En carreteras secundarias reviradas mantiene bien controlada la carrocería y, cuando el firme empeora, conserva suficiente recorrido para no resultar agotador. La perfecta compañera de viaje es, sin duda, la dirección. Tiene un tacto directo y transmite con precisión las órdenes que damos al volante. No llega a sobrecargar al conductor como lo hacen algunos deportivos clásicos, pero sí proporciona una conexión mucho más natural con el eje delantero que aquella a la que nos están acostumbrando los modelos chinos. El morro responde con rapidez y el coche se coloca con facilidad, haciendo que los 4,05 metros de carrocería y la batalla de 2,60 metros jueguen claramente a su favor. Es ahí donde el VZ consigue ofrecer algo más gracias al diferencial electrónico y a sus neumáticos más anchos. Al acelerar muy pronto desde el vértice, su capacidad para repartir mejor la fuerza disponible le permite aprovechar con mayor eficacia los 226 CV. El Endurance manda sus 211 CV y 290 Nm exclusivamente al eje delantero, pero, en una utilización normal e incluso a un ritmo bastante elevado, la motricidad resulta convincente. Para empezar a echar realmente en falta el e-LSD hay que exigirle al coche mucho más de lo que será habitual en carretera abierta. Eso explica por qué esta versión nos parece tan bien resuelta. La diferencia de potencia respecto al VZ es de apenas 15 CV y el 0 a 100 km/h pasa de 6,8 a 7,1 segundos. En el 0 a 50 km/h ambos necesitan 3,1 segundos, mientras que el Endurance recupera de 80 a 120 km/h en 4,2 segundos. En otras palabras, al adelantar o incorporarnos a una autovía no existe esa sensación de estar conduciendo el Raval lento. Todo lo contrario. Ahí es donde el nuevo motor APP290 síncrono de imanes permanentes entra en juego. Más allá de las cifras, entrega la potencia de forma inmediata, aunque CUPRA no ha querido que su respuesta sea excesivamente violenta en los primeros metros de acelerador. Hay fuerza desde abajo y las recuperaciones son rápidas, aunque la entrega sigue siendo suficientemente progresiva como para dosificarla con precisión. Al seleccionar los perfiles más deportivos cambia de manera perceptible la respuesta del acelerador y aparece el sonido artificial desarrollado por CUPRA, que acompaña la ganancia de velocidad dentro del habitáculo, ayudando a romper esa monotonía acústica habitual de un eléctrico cuando decidimos aumentar el ritmo. Puede desconectarse y probablemente habrá conductores que prefieran hacerlo, pero, en un puerto de montaña y con el carácter que transmite el coche, la simbiosis resulta bastante mejor que la que suelen ofrecer otros sistemas de sonido sintéticos. También funcionan especialmente bien las levas situadas detrás del volante, convirtiéndose en un detalle casi propio de la marca (el ID. Polo carece de ellas, no en vano). No solo permiten modificar la retención sin necesidad de tener que toquetear la pantalla central y aprovechar la regeneración de forma bastante intuitiva, sino que acaban por convertirse en una extensión de las sensaciones deportivas, pues, si bien no cambias de relación, sí aportan el dinamismo suficiente para aumentar el ritmo y decelerar antes de una curva con más decisión. A ello se suma un modo One Pedal capaz de aumentar todavía más la retención en ciudad, el cual se activa a través del selector del cambio. Y ojo, porque el tacto del pedal del freno es mucho más natural que en otros eléctricos, algo que quizá se deba en parte a que ahora los cuatro frenos son de disco y a que el sistema one-box combina recuperación y frenada hidráulica. El tacto resulta progresivo y facilita dosificar bien la frenada, algo que sigue sin estar igualmente conseguido en todos los eléctricos. Más allá de esta semejanza frente al VZ, donde realmente le saca ventaja el Endurance es cuando toca pensar en el uso cotidiano. Porque ambos comparten la misma batería NMC de 52 kWh netos, logrando aquí homologar hasta 446 kilómetros dependiendo de la configuración. Es, por tanto, el Raval con mayor autonomía. La diferencia de casi 60 km frente al VZ se debe, principalmente, a que este último monta unos neumáticos de altas prestaciones. Cierto es que puede alcanzar los 440 km escogiendo sin coste adicional otras gomas de mayor eficiencia, pero incluso en esa configuración el Endurance conserva una ligera ventaja. En cuanto a nuestra experiencia de conducción, si bien alternamos muchos tramos de montaña, lo cierto es que, en un recorrido mixto, con tramos de autovía a 120 km/h y mucho desnivel, el Raval Endurance se movió en torno a los 17,2 kWh/100 km, pudiendo bajar a menos de 14 kWh/100 km en zonas urbanas. Con ello, el rango real podría estar rozando los 400 kilómetros sin apenas problemas, contando con margen suficiente para salir de la ciudad. En este sentido, la potencia de carga se mantiene igual y, en corriente continua, admite conexiones de 105 kW, con las que CUPRA anuncia 24 minutos para pasar del 10 al 80 %. En corriente alterna admite 11 kW y necesita unas cinco horas y media para completar la batería. Cierto es que algunos rivales admiten potencias superiores, aunque la capacidad relativamente contenida del acumulador evita que los tiempos de espera se disparen. Con todo, llegamos al punto que quizá decante la balanza. Porque CUPRA anuncia oficialmente el Raval Endurance por 35.010 euros, una tarifa que no está sujeta a promociones, descuentos ni ayudas. Ello implica ser 4.060 euros más económico que el Raval VZ, que parte de los 39.070 euros. Una diferencia que puede ser pequeña o grande dependiendo de las necesidades de cada uno, pero que en la práctica puede justificarse ante un coche que únicamente cede 15 CV y tres décimas en el 0 a 100 km/h, al tiempo que gana autonomía y conserva buena parte de las cualidades que hacen especialmente interesante al chasis del Raval. Ahora bien, con todos los descuentos y bonificaciones, la tarifa de este Raval Endurance se queda en los 25.490 euros, provocando a buen seguro que muchos usuarios se permitan sacrificar ciertos elementos por tener un modelo tan llamativo y deportivo como democratizador. A falta de conducir el Plus, que reduce la potencia hasta los 135 CV y la autonomía a 328 kilómetros, el Endurance es el Raval que mejor equilibra las diferentes facetas del coche.

articles.title: Los Pou vuelven a dejar su huella en los Picos de Europa
articles.standfirst: Iker y Eneko completan en libre ‘Vicios Ocultos’, la vía de 285 metros y dificultad 7c que abrieron el año pasado en el Tiro Pedabejo
articles.summary: Iker y Eneko completan en libre ‘Vicios Ocultos’, la vía de 285 metros y dificultad 7c que abrieron el año pasado en el Tiro Pedabejo
articles.body: Iker y Eneko Pou volvieron a los Picos de Europa para completar una tarea que tenían pendiente. Los alaveses completaron la primera escalada en libre de ‘Vicios Ocultos’, una vía de 285 metros y dificultad máxima de 7c que ellos mismos abrieron el año pasado en el Tiro Pedabejo, una cumbre de 2.189 metros situada entre el valle leonés de Valdeón y el cántabro de Liébana. La vía está dividida en seis largos y los Pou destacan especialmente la calidad de la roca y el trazado: "Es una de las más bonitas que hemos hecho en estas montañas. La línea es genial, la calidad de la roca notable y cuenta con seis largos de mucha clase", explica Iker. La ruta tiene cierta exposición, aunque los hermanos consideran que su dificultad, sin ser máxima, puede hacer que con el tiempo se convierta en una vía de referencia en la zona. "Estamos seguros de que al no ser una dificultad extrema, con el tiempo se acabará convirtiendo en una gran clásica", añade. La graduación de la vía queda, de momento y a la espera de futuras repeticiones, en L1: 5+, L2: 7c, L3: 7a+, L4: 7b, L5: 7a y L6: 6b. No era la primera vez que los Pou trabajaban en el Tiro Pedabejo. En 2019, Iker, junto a Jon Gurutz Lazkoz y Kiko Cerdá, abrió y escaló en libre ‘Dardara’, una vía de 200 metros con dificultades de 7c+/8a. Como ya ocurrió durante la apertura del año pasado, los Pou necesitaron dos jornadas completas para terminar el trabajo. La primera la compartieron con su amigo sudtirolés Mathias Senfter. "No pudimos liberar todos los largos, por lo que hubo un segundo día- desgraciadamente ya sin Mathias que tenía que volver a casa- en el que nos empleamos a fondo para acabar la faena", relata Eneko Pou. Esta vez, además, no tuvieron que afrontar ningún momento especialmente delicado. Durante la apertura del año pasado, un bloque se movió cuando Eneko estaba terminando el cuarto largo y estuvo cerca de sufrir una caída de entre 30 y 40 metros. Completar en libre las vías que abren es una parte importante de la forma de entender la escalada de los Pou. Para ellos supone afrontar dos trabajos diferentes sobre una misma línea. "Se convierte en un doble trabajo, pero de esta manera tenemos la sensación de conseguir el 10 en el examen. Lo hemos hecho en nuestras rutas más importantes por todo el mundo, y también, por supuesto, en nuestros queridos Picos de Europa, en líneas tan significativas como 'Orbayu', 'Rayu', 'Lurgorri'..., explica Iker, el pequeño de los Pou. El nombre de ‘Vicios Ocultos’ surgió durante una cena con las amigas del refugio La Ardilla Real, en Santa Marina de Valdeón. Los Pou quisieron así dedicarles la vía después de las jornadas que compartieron con ellas durante la apertura. "Era una manera de dedicarles la vía tras unas jornadas memorables en su compañía, en este precioso lugar de la montaña leonesa que tanto queremos", cuenta Iker. La nueva vía se suma a un año especialmente activo para los Pou. A principios de verano completaron en los Andes peruanos ‘Bonustrack’, una de sus actividades más importantes en alpinismo hasta la fecha. También cumplieron uno de sus objetivos pendientes con el ascenso al Alpamayo.

articles.title: Super League Grand Final will be a special family affair for Sir Kevin Sinfield and son Jack at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Sir Kevin Sinfield's son Jack Sinfield will play in his first Grand Final on Saturday and his dad will deliver the match ball; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm
articles.body:
Sinfield is the son of Sir Kevin Sinfield MBE who is in the middle of his latest gruelling running endeavour, running seven ultra marathons in seven days stopping at all 12 English Super League clubs along the way.

Kevin Sinfield has helped raise more than £11m for the MND community with his team since his first annual challenge in 2020.

He will finish his final challenge by coming out to onto the Old Trafford pitch and delivering the match ball with his son, Jack, who will be gearing up to play in his first ever Super League final.

Wakefield take on Warrington Wolves to make history and become the sixth-ever Super League winner, live on Sky Sports on Saturday October 3.

All at once, the Wakefield man will have overwhelming pride in his dad, the nerves of the biggest moment of his career, and the pressure of trying to emulate all the wins on that hallowed turf that his dad pulled off with Leeds.

Jack Sinfield has been missing his dad while he has been away and knows you could not write the outcome that has happened with their journeys colliding at the Theatre of Dreams.

"I've spoke to him (dad) a little bit, but obviously he's been really tired. I think I've said already that when he planned this last challenge and for it to finish at Old Trafford, I don't think even he could have imagined that I would be playing in it. So it's worked out pretty well," Jack Sinfield said.

"It was really nice to see him. I've obviously missed him a lot when he's been away because I'm still living at home, so it's really weird around the house without him.

"I'm hoping I'll see him on Thursday when he goes past home and he runs up near our neck of the woods."

From childhood memories to career highlights: Emulating dad

Old Trafford is not a new place to Jack as he spent his childhood watching his dad, the Leeds Rhinos legend win the Super League on seven occasions.

He has cherished memories of his dad's career highlights and now knows it is his moment to try and "emulate" him.

"My first ever rugby league game was the 2004 Grand Final when I was three weeks old. I have been to every single one of the Grand Finals my dad has played in but the last one really stands out in 2015," he added.

"I had just turned 11 then so that's the one I really remember the most, knowing it was his last game as well. Obviously it was really emotional for us all as a family and that's the main memory I have that really sticks out, especially with it being the game where Leeds won the treble.

"I didn't realise how stressful it was trying to sort tickets, I've seen my dad do it for years. The last two days have been carnage trying to sort everything out. But it's worth it, these are the games you want to be playing in, so it's all worth it.

"It's been a dream of mine to go there one day and emulate him and win one. But now it's here, it's definitely feeling a bit different.

"I've got that picture on my phone still. It was a pretty special moment - hopefully there will be a chance to have another picture this weekend.. I'd want him to have a shower first though."

Indeed, the player of the match award is now called the Rob Burrow Award. Imagine the fairy-tale if Sinfield senior watches his son win the trophy named after his mate who has inspired all the charity work he has taken on. Who inspired a sport. Who inspired a nation.

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will take place at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.

articles.title: La asignatura pendiente del deporte en la adolescencia: las mujeres lo dejan más y antes que ellos
articles.standfirst: Sólo el 23% de las adolescentes llegan al nivel de actividad física pautado por la OMS, por un 49% de los chicos. El factor competitivo y los estereotipos sociales, algunas de las causas
articles.summary: Sólo el 23% de las adolescentes llegan al nivel de actividad física pautado por la OMS, por un 49% de los chicos. El factor competitivo y los estereotipos sociales, algunas de las causas
articles.body: Aunque la última Encuesta de Hábitos Deportivos, elaborada por el Ministerio de Educación, Formación Profesional y Deportes junto al CSD, señala que la brecha de género en la práctica deportiva se ha reducido hasta mínimos históricos -un 66,2% de los hombres realiza actividad física frente al 59,5% de mujeres-, la adolescencia se presenta como el momento crítico en el que se produce la mayor tasa de abandono deportivo por parte de las féminas. Diversas señales de alarma, como el aumento del sedentarismo y el incremento por parte de los adolescentes del uso de las pantallas, llevó a los expertos a realizar distintos estudios para analizar el porqué las niñas, que en edad infantil practican una actividad física similar a los chicos, son las que más renuncian al deporte cuando alcanzan la pubertad. "Lo primero que apreciamos es que este abandono de la actividad física es mayor y se produce antes entre las chicas que entre los chicos, sobre todo en España", asegura a MARCA María Martín, Doctora en Ciencias de la Actividad Física y el Deporte y directora del 'Proyecto I+D+i Actividades físicas y deportivas para las adolescentes: Necesidades, barreras y recomendaciones', estudio realizado por la Facultad CAFYD (INEF) de la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, en colaboración con la Fundación MAPFRE y el Consejo COLEF. "Queríamos ver qué deporte hacen y qué les gustaría hacer. Y los resultados revelaron que 7 de cada 10 chicas quieren moverse más y mejor, pero tienen más barreras, muros a los que ellos no tienen que enfrentarse". Como en la mayoría de los fenómenos sociales, la casuística es multifactorial y no depende de una única circunstancia. Los datos de este estudio recogen que el doble de chicos (49%) que de chicas (23%) alcanzan el nivel vinculado a las recomendaciones de actividad física pautadas por la Organización Mundial de la Salud (2020) y un 26,6% de las adolescentes (12,3% en los chicos) se encuadran directamente en el nivel sedentario. "Esas barreras tienen que ver con la oferta y las oportunidades, como las instalaciones o la autonomía", explica María Martín. "La oferta sigue privilegiando lo mejor y lo masculino. Y en la adolescencia eso se traduce, sobre todo, en la competición. Todos buscan disfrutar, divertirse y sentirse mejor con la actividad física, pero el modelo está más centrado en la competición y menos en la salud". El deporte competitivo tiene una presencia relevante en la adolescencia. El 61% de chicos y 36% de chicas practican de forma semanal un deporte orientado a la competición. Pero a ellos les motiva más competir (43% por 18%). Eso se traduce en que aquellas adolescentes que quieren practicar deporte por otras razones, como la socialización y la salud, ven penalizada su oferta. Además en esta etapa desaparecen los equipos mixtos y los que se forman nacen para la competición. En la etapa de Secundaria, además, los adolescentes necesitan dedicar más tiempo a los estudios, pero ellas cuentan con menos oferta deportiva dirigida de proximidad. Si deben desplazarse más lejos para hacer una actividad física, lo que requiere más tiempo y apoyo familiar, muchas priorizan los estudios en detrimento del deporte. El estudio también demostró que hay diferencias en el tipo de actividades realizadas: los chicos apuestan por el fútbol (57%), mientras que las chicas optan por pasear (40%). Ellos practican más balompié, baloncesto, tenis, pádel, bicicleta, carrera y musculación, mientras que las adolescentes se decantan por pasear, el baile, patinaje, voleibol y gimnasia rítmica. En la elección de las actividades también influye el tipo de instalaciones en las que se practican. Los chicos ocupan mayoritariamente los espacios colectivos de práctica y recintos deportivos. Una de las razones es porque son espacios que se dedican a la competición y otra, porque las chicas no se encuentran cómodas en muchos de ellos. "Aquí vimos algo que no aparece en estudios realizados en otros países", analiza María Martín. "Las chicas hablan a veces de intimidación, incluso miedo. Se sienten expulsadas, van a instalaciones en las que no se encuentran a gusto. Ahí confluyen barreras, como falta de seguridad, vergüenza..." Hay que recordar que en la adolescencia hay cambios físicos importantes, como la llegada de la menstruación, y también psicológicos, en los que ciertos estereotipos arcaicos de feminidad pueden afectar a las adolescentes. "Esas presiones estéticas que aún existen, como estar delgada, si estás musculada se deduce que no es un cuerpo femenino..., ellos no las tienen", apunta María Martín. "Tenemos referentes en el deporte de élite pero en la oferta hay que presentar cuerpos diversos, no normativos, con discapacidad... Debe haber profesionales con formación. Es importante lo que se hace pero también cómo se hace". Esos prejuicios físicos, algunos de los cuales aún se perpetúan, los recuerdan deportistas de élite, como Teresa Portela, subcampeona olímpica de K1 200, y Lucía Martín-Portugués. "Hace 30 años, cuando yo empezaba, no era tan normal que las chicas hicieran deporte", asegura a MARCA Teresa Portela. "En piragüismo, que necesitas fuerza y desarrollas musculatura, hubo algún caso de madres que recomendaron a sus hijas no seguir en esa disciplina porque no se adecuaba a ciertos cánones de feminidad. Pero creo que eso ahora ha cambiado". También Lucía Martín Portugués aseguró en una entrevista en MARCA que "durante la adolescencia fue terrible porque yo estaba fuerte, tenía abdominales, las piernas fuertes y llegué a pasar hasta por un TCA (Trastorno de Conducta Alimentaria) porque no me paraban de llegar comentarios de todo el mundo diciéndote que tienes cuerpo de hombre. Y lo que tenía era un cuerpo atlético". Para promover la continuidad de la actividad física entre las adolescentes, desde este grupo de investigación psicosocial en el deporte de la Facultad de Ciencias de la Actividad Física y del Deporte se elaboró una guía con recomendaciones para los distintos actores del ámbito deportivo, desde la familia a entrenadores y organismos. Con el centro escolar como agente clave que promueva esa práctica, hay que desarrollar modelos dirigidos a adolescentes en los que el deporte de competición conviva también con la práctica saludable. Otro de los objetivos es cambiar el paradigma de las instalaciones deportivas, con espacios recreativos más amigables para las adolescentes. "Se deben hacer campañas de sensibilización y fomento de la actividad física con el que ellas se identifiquen, que digan 'esto también es para mí'", explica María Martín. También la educación es importante, con las redes sociales como uno de los vehículos más importante para llegar a los más jóvenes. "Ellas construyen su imaginario a través de las redes, por eso deberían mostrar cuerpos diversos". Estos datos de abandono del deporte entre las adolescentes son comunes en otros países de Europa. En Reino Unido, por ejemplo, encuestas realizadas en 2025 mostraron que el 64% de las niñas dejan de practicar actividad física al final de la pubertad, una problemática que llegó incluso al Parlamento. Allí, Tanni Grey-Thompson, exatleta paralímpica con múltiples medallas en los Juegos y parlamentaria, aseguró en una comisión que "lo realmente importante es que tengamos una generación de mujeres en forma y saludables y el 80 % no está lo suficientemente en forma para estarlo, debido a todas las barreras que ya conocemos para la participación". Las estadísticas se repiten en Francia, que contabilizó la caída drástica en las licencias entre las adolescentes. En la temporada 2023-2024, 831.085 niñas de entre 10 y 14 años estaban licenciadas por una Federación olímpica, mientras que en el grupo de edad de 15 a 19 años, esta cifra se redujo a tan sólo 374.653, según recogió L'Equipe, algo que no ocurre entre los niños en la misma proporción.

articles.title: 'Real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh lead cricket fraternity in hailing Captain Smit Machchhar after saving 174 lives
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073, has earned admiration from across the country, including some of India's biggest cricketing names.Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag were among the former India cricketers who took to social media to salute Machchhar for his bravery and presence of mind during the terrifying mid-air incident.Machchhar was the captain of the Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight when a violent confrontation reportedly broke out in the cockpit on Wednesday. According to reports, he was attacked by his co-pilot but, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to help open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene. The aircraft was subsequently diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 174 people aboard were reported safe.'A true real-life hero': Sachin TendulkarTendulkar was among the first prominent cricketers to acknowledge Machchhar's courage."Learnt about the incredible bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar. Immense courage in the face of a terrifying and unprecedented challenge. A true real-life hero. The entire world is proud of you," Tendulkar wrote.Raina hails 'son of Gujarat'Former India batter Suresh Raina also paid tribute to Machchhar, highlighting the captain's courage despite being seriously injured."A true hero, a proud moment for India! Salute to Captain Smit Machchhar, a son of Gujarat, whose extraordinary courage and presence of mind, even while seriously injured, helped save 174 precious lives," Raina wrote.Sehwag praises his courage under pressureVirender Sehwag highlighted the extraordinary circumstances in which Machchhar continued to act despite his injuries."In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," Sehwag wrote.Yuvraj: 'Some moments show you what a person is truly made of'Yuvraj Singh also joined the tributes, focusing on Machchhar's decision to put the safety of others ahead of his own."Some moments show you what a person is truly made of," Yuvraj wrote.Machchhar, who has more than 13 years of commercial flying experience and previously worked with SpiceJet before joining flydubai in 2022, is currently recovering after undergoing treatment in Saudi Arabia.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why did Ronaldo leave Portugal’s training camp, and will he play again?
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo left after Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus held a news conference. Al Jazeera explains what happened.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s abrupt departure from Portugal’s training camp ahead of their fixture against hosts Denmark has prompted a string of questions and a few answers.

The global superstar’s exit on Wednesday was preceded by an explosive revelation by head coach Jorge Jesus, who said Ronaldo would not be picked for Portugal’s Nations League match against Denmark.

The UEFA Nations League title holders will now take to the field in Copenhagen, Denmark, without their talismanic captain on matchday three of the competition.

What happened between Ronaldo and Portugal coach Jesus?

Ronaldo left Portugal’s training camp after a dispute with Jesus on the eve of their Nations League match against Denmark. The 41-year-old captain had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s news conference.

Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would train as normal. However, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his teammates on the pitch.

Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving Parken alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus’s news conference. They also said that Ronaldo’s private jet was heading to Copenhagen. Spanish sports media ⁠⁠⁠⁠outlet Marca reported that Ronaldo intended to board a private flight to Madrid in the coming hours.

The Portuguese Football ⁠⁠⁠⁠Federation (FPF) confirmed Ronaldo had left the camp but said preparations for the match against Denmark and Sunday’s home game against Norway would continue as planned with the remaining 24 players.

The Portugal squad later arrived at their ‌‌‌‌hotel without Ronaldo and without Jesus, with the whereabouts ‌‌‌‌of ‌‌‌‌both still unknown.

The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’s Nations League clash away to Denmark, either.

Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.

Ronaldo reacted on social media soon after his departure from the camp.

“Following the national team manager’s press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I ⁠⁠⁠⁠have decided to leave ⁠⁠⁠⁠the national team’s training camp,” he wrote on Instagram.

“In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.”

“Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”

Jesus initially denied that Ronaldo had left the camp before the FPF and Ronaldo confirmed otherwise.

He also addressed Ronaldo’s decision to head straight to the changing rooms instead of celebrating with the team after their 2-1 victory over Norway.

“There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus told reporters. “Any player — and I was a player myself… when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on … no one is happy about that,” Jesus said on Wednesday.

The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting lineup, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.

“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted.

The former Benfica boss also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical “mobility” and “strengthening”.

Has Ronaldo ever left a camp like this before?

No. This is the first time Ronaldo has stormed out of a training camp in his 23 years of playing for Portugal.

Which other famous players have left their national teams or been sent home?

Ronaldo’s departure was relatively subdued compared with the infamous Saipan incident in 2002 involving Roy Keane, captain of the Republic of Ireland, and manager Mick McCarthy ahead of the World Cup in Japan and South Korea.

Keane was vociferous about unsatisfactory training conditions in Saipan, for which McCarthy demanded an apology at a team meeting days later.

Keane reportedly lambasted him with the saying: “I didn’t rate you as a player, I don’t rate you as a manager, and I don’t rate you as a person”, before storming off the pitch. He never played at the World Cup and said he would not play again for Ireland under McCarthy.

Eight years later, at the FIFA World Cup 2010, France forward Nicolas Anelka was expelled from the national team for an explosive, expletive-laden tirade against head coach Raymond Domenech during half-time in France’s group-stage match against Mexico.

The French Football Federation (FFF) sent Anelka home after he refused to apologise to Domenech. In turn, the French squad boycotted training for a day, saying the FFF “did not at any time try to protect the group.” The FFF’s managing director subsequently quit.

Has Ronaldo played his last game for Portugal?

Ronaldo fuelled speculation about his retirement plans after saying⁠⁠ in August that the upcoming ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠year will probably be the last of his playing career.

“This is probably my last year of football and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo told lifestyle magazine Vogue.

The forward has scored 976 ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠goals for club and country during a ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠career spanning more than two decades. Ronaldo will continue playing for Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌this ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌season as he closes in on a milestone of 1,000 career goals.

articles.title: Abhishek strikes with 45 seconds left as India pip Pakistan 4-3 to enter Asian Games hockey gold-medal match
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India survived a huge scare against Pakistan before Abhishek scored with just 45 seconds left to give the defending champions a dramatic 4-3
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India survived a huge scare against Pakistan before Abhishek scored with just 45 seconds left to give the defending champions a dramatic 4-3 win in the Asian Games hockey semifinal on Thursday.The victory sends India into the hockey gold medal match, while Pakistan will play for the bronze medal.India will take on the winner of the second semifinal between Malaysia and Korea.Just when the semifinal looked set for a shootout, Abhishek produced the winning moment. His effort took a deflection off Pakistan defender Sufiyan and went past goalkeeper Ali Raza to send India into the gold-medal match.India will face the winner of the second semifinal between South Korea and Malaysia.Harmanpreet puts India in controlIndia started on the front foot and kept Pakistan under pressure from the opening minutes.After failing to convert their first four penalty corners, India finally broke the deadlock in the fifth minute. Captain Harmanpreet stepped up and fired a powerful drag-flick past goalkeeper Ali Raza to make it 1-0.Harmanpreet struck again in the 13th minute. Manpreet Singh's run down the left helped India win their seventh penalty corner, and the captain made no mistake.India were now firmly in control and Pakistan struggled to find a way into the game.Sukhjeet then made it 3-0 in the 23rd minute. Shilanand Lakra sent a fine pass from the left of the goal-line and Sukhjeet finished the move.India appeared to have one foot in the final.Pakistan find a way backPakistan, however, got a much-needed goal just before half-time.Abu Mahmood scored from a penalty corner in the 30th minute to reduce the deficit to 1-3 and give Pakistan hope.India continued to attack after the break. Dilpreet Singh and Hardik Singh helped India create chances, while Abhishek came close to scoring in the 40th minute when his flick hit the far post.That miss soon became important.Pakistan grew in confidence and started putting India's defence under pressure. Hannan Shahid scored in the 45th minute after receiving a pass from Ali Ghazanfar to make it 2-3.The goal changed the mood of the match. Pakistan were suddenly on top, while India struggled to regain control.Pakistan complete the comebackIndia were forced to play with 10 men for a period after Dilpreet was shown a green card in the 43rd minute.Pakistan used the opportunity to keep attacking and eventually found the equaliser.Hannan set up Waheed Rana in the 49th minute and Rana finished the chance to make it 3-3.From being three goals ahead, India were suddenly facing the possibility of a shootout.Pakistan continued to push forward in the final stages, while India were forced to defend deep. The Indian defence and goalkeeper made important saves to keep the score level.India also had a video referral for a penalty corner, but the appeal was turned down.Abhishek has the final sayWith the clock running down, India finally found their moment.Abhishek got his stick to the ball near the goalmouth with just 45 seconds remaining. The ball took a deflection off Sufiyan and wrong-footed Ali Raza before finding the back of the net.India had their 4-3 lead back.Pakistan tried to find another equaliser in the final seconds, but India held on to complete a dramatic victory.The defending champions had dominated the first half and built a 3-0 lead, but Pakistan's three-goal comeback exposed India's struggles after the break.In the end, Abhishek's late goal ensured India avoided a shootout and booked their place in the Asian Games hockey gold-medal match.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India to face Pakistan in Asian Games men’s cricket final
articles.summary: India defeated Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the semifinal to book their spot in a first-ever games clash with Pakistan.
articles.body:
India humiliated a second-string Sri Lanka side by 124 runs at the Asian Games to book a gold-medal decider against rivals Pakistan in the T20 cricket event, marking the first time the two sides will meet at the games.

The day after India’s depleted one-day international team completed the second-highest successful chase in an eight-wicket win over the West Indies, Shreyas Iyer’s T20 side dismissed Sri Lanka for 45 in 9.5 overs at Korogi Athletic Park on Thursday after setting them a target of 170.

Pace supremo Jasprit Bumrah (2-7) set the tone with two wickets in the first five balls, trapping Sineth Jayawardena lbw for a duck and having number three Sohan de Livera caught behind for nought.

Panicky opener Lasith Croospulle was then run out with a ludicrous dash for a single as Sri Lanka slumped to three for two.

Two more run-outs followed as Sri Lanka collapsed on a warm and sunny afternoon, with number four Nuwanidu Fernando, the second innings’ top scorer, out for 15.

Left-arm spinner Abhishek Sharma finished with 2-2 from five balls.

India were not overly impressive in their own batting against outgunned opponents, but Ishan Kishan smashed an unbeaten 80 from 46 balls to anchor their innings and opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 38.

In the earlier semifinal, middle-order batter Abdul Samad blasted an unbeaten 30 off 15 balls to help Pakistan to a six-wicket win over Bangladesh in a match reduced to 13 overs a side due to a wet outfield.

Towhid Hridoy made 42 as Bangladesh set an imposing 112 for victory in the shortened match, with Pakistan’s left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim taking 3-26.

All four semifinalists qualified by virtue of their international rankings, with their respective quarterfinals abandoned due to rain.

India will bid for back-to-back men’s cricket titles, three years after taking the gold in Hangzhou courtesy of the ranking rule when their final against Afghanistan was abandoned due to rain.

Earlier, Indian women defended their title as Sri Lanka settled for silver once again, while Pakistan defeated Bangladesh for bronze.

The blockbuster clash has been headlined by the infamous question of whether there will be a customary handshake after political tensions between India and Pakistan have spilled onto the pitch in the past year.

Then-Indian captain Suryakumar Yadav and his players refused to shake hands with Pakistani team members during an Asia Cup clash in September last year, deciding not to accept the trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi, who also serves as Pakistan’s interior minister.

When Pakistan faced India in the ICC Women’s World Cup 2025 in Sri Lanka, the teams steered clear of handshakes and repeated the practice at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup earlier this year in England, as well as their group-stage match in the Women’s Asia Cup.

Last month, the India women’s team refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi after winning the Asia Cup final in Dubai, UAE.

articles.title: Who can Anthony Joshua face next if he beats Tyson Fury in blockbuster WBA ‘super’ heavyweight title showdown on December 11
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua has already named his preferred next opponent if he defeats Tyson Fury in their long-awaited heavyweight showdown.
articles.body: Anthony Joshua has already named his preferred next opponent if he defeats Tyson Fury in their long-awaited heavyweight showdown. Joshua and Fury are scheduled to meet on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, with the WBA ‘super’ heavyweight title reportedly at stake. After years of failed negotiations, the two British rivals will finally settle their rivalry in the ring.But Joshua could already have another heavyweight champion in his sights. When asked which champion he would want to face after Fury, Joshua gave a clear answer: Murat Gassiev. The Russian currently holds the WBA heavyweight title and could become an important part of Joshua’s plans if the British star wins on December 11.Why does Anthony Joshua want Murat Gassiev next?Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will have much more than bragging rights on the line when they meet in Cardiff. Reports have stated that the WBA ‘super’ heavyweight belt will be awarded to the winner.If confirmed, it would be an unusual situation in the heavyweight division. The title would be contested by two fighters who currently do not hold a world championship.That situation has created a problem for Murat Gassiev.The Russian became the sole WBA heavyweight champion after Oleksandr Usyk gave up his world titles in June. Gassiev had previously held the WBA’s secondary ‘regular’ championship. With no ‘super’ champion in the division, however, his position effectively became the WBA’s main heavyweight title.Gassiev defended his championship in July against short-notice replacement Peter Kadiru. He later learned through a report from Ring Magazine that his title status could be changed to make room for Joshua and Fury.Gassiev said he had not received official confirmation from the WBA as of Tuesday. His team then filed a formal objection.“If anyone should be fighting for the WBA Super heavyweight title, it is Murat Gassiev, the reigning champion, not two boxers who currently hold no world title between them,” wrote John Wirt, co-promoter and legal counsel for Gassiev.Fury has since confirmed that the WBA ‘super’ title has been sanctioned for his fight with Joshua. However, the belt was not discussed during Wednesday’s press conference.Joshua was later asked who he would like to fight if he gets past Fury. His answer was “Murat Gassiev.”That response could create an interesting path for Joshua after December 11.Under WBA rules, a ‘super’ champion is generally expected to defend against the ‘regular’ champion within 18 months. If Joshua wins the WBA ‘super’ belt, Gassiev could therefore become a potential mandatory opponent.However, the rule has not always been strictly followed, particularly in the heavyweight division.Mahmoud Charr is one example. He held the WBA ‘regular’ heavyweight title for five consecutive years without facing the ‘super’ champion in a unification bout.That means Joshua naming Gassiev does not automatically guarantee that the two fighters will meet.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La Federación de Triatlón nunca se planteó suspender la Copa de Europa en Ceuta
articles.standfirst: Se disputa este domingo con casi 100 triatletas de 23 países
articles.summary: Se disputa este domingo con casi 100 triatletas de 23 países
articles.body: El director de competiciones de la Federación Española de Triatlón (FETRI), Jorge García, aseguró este jueves que nunca "hubo dudas" sobre la posibilidad de suspender la prueba la Copa de Europa en la modalidad de esprint que albergará Ceuta el próximo domingo, pese a la crisis migratoria por la que atraviesa la ciudad. El dirigente de la FETRI destacó que es un "buen momento" para dar a conocer la "verdadera imagen" de Ceuta tras la crisis que surgió a finales del pasado julio, cuando miles de personas cruzaron irregularmente la frontera de la ciudad desde Marruecos. Jorge García expresó este deseo durante la presentación oficial de la prueba que se disputará el domingo por quinto año consecutivo en la ciudad autónoma y que reunirá a cerca de un centenar de triatletas de mas de una veintena de países, de ellos 66 en la categoría masculina y 32 en la femenina. "Desde el primer minuto que se produjo la crisis siempre se mantuvo el compromiso de la ciudad con el triatlón, en Ceuta estamos como en nuestra casa, la ciudadanía es ejemplar y siempre tuvimos claro que se iba a celebrar", ha afirmado García junto a la gerente del Instituto Ceutí de Deportes, Araceli García, y el presidente de la Federación de Triatlón de Ceuta, Jorge Ruiz. La crisis migratoria no ha afectado a la inscripción "ya que los números son similares a los de años anteriores y son lo habitual en este tipo de competiciones", añadió García, quien destacó que están "donde hay que estar y los deportistas, que siempre se han ido de Ceuta hablando maravillas, se sienten en deuda con la ciudad y aquí volverán". Jorge García insistió en que es una "buena oportunidad" para la proyección exterior de la imagen de Ceuta ya que la prueba se retransmitirá en directo durante dos horas por Teledeporte, además de que el apoyo de la institución 'Europe Triatlón' con la ciudad se ha concretado con la designación de Ceuta para acoger en 2027 el Campeonato de Europa de Triatlón Esprint. "Vamos a demostrar cómo es Ceuta y su imagen, aquí las cosas siempre se han hecho bien y esperamos que el público vuelva a responder como siempre lo ha hecho", advirtió Jorge García, quien subrayó, en el plano deportivo, que entre los españoles hay varios que pueden optar al podio "aunque hay mucha igualdad en las listas de salida". La gerente del Instituto Ceutí de Deportes, por su parte, agradeció el apoyo de la FETRI y de la Europe Triatlón porque "es una oportunidad para proyectar la imagen de Ceuta y mostrar la capacidad para organizar eventos internacionales con todas las garantías". Además, animó a los ciudadanos a "llenar" las calles en la matinal del domingo para mostrar su respaldo a esta prueba.

articles.title: Mirabai Chanu keeps injury worries at bay, sets sights on elusive Asian Games medal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, the Asian Games have become the one unfinished chapter in an otherwise glittering career.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, the Asian Games have become the one unfinished chapter in an otherwise glittering career. The Tokyo Olympics silver medallist has collected medals at every major global competition she has contested, but an Asian Games podium finish has continued to elude her.With the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games beginning on September 19, staying fit has become as important as lifting big weights for the 32-year-old. And Mirabai has leaned on a familiar support system, with coach Vijay Sharma overseeing her training at the Modinagar base and American strength and conditioning coach Dr Aaron Horschig providing regular input.The association with Horschig dates back to November 2020, and the two continue to hold a video call every Thursday to review Mirabai's training and recovery."We have a video call every Thursday with him and we discuss everything about training, recovery and the next steps. Everything is reviewed to the finest detail. Since Dr Horschig was a weightlifter himself, he knows every muscle in the body. This constant review has kept me in shape," Mirabai told SAI Media.The determination to crack the Asian Games code has also meant sacrificing time away from home. Mirabai returned from Glasgow after winning her third Commonwealth Games gold and went straight back to training in Modinagar. She did not even travel to her home state of Manipur."I did not go home (in Manipur) and I have set myself a challenge — no going home till I win a medal at the Asian Games," she said.Her Asian Games history explains the obsession. At Hangzhou in 2023, Mirabai finished fourth in the 49kg category after a hip and thigh injury disrupted her campaign during the snatch. Four years earlier in Jakarta, she missed the Games altogether because of a serious back injury.This time, the focus has been firmly on keeping her body in shape."We have been careful with fitness and so far, I have felt good with my body," she said.Mirabai's latest Commonwealth Games triumph in Glasgow offered further evidence of her consistency, although she does not believe it was a particularly demanding contest. She lifted 190kg in total — 85kg in the snatch and 105kg in the clean and jerk — to win the women's 48kg gold and set new Commonwealth Games records in all three categories."The competition in the Commonwealth Games was not tough for me. I did not have to put in a lot of effort at Glasgow. The real test lies ahead," she said.That test will come in Japan, where Mirabai expects a dramatically stronger field. Chinese, North Korean, Japanese and Thai lifters are among those she expects to pose the biggest challenge.At the Paris Olympics last year, Thailand's Surodchana Khambao finished ahead of Mirabai by just one kilogram, lifting 200kg to take third place while the Indian finished fourth."My personal best is 205kg (89+116kg). I want to see how far I can go in Japan. The Asian Games have been the toughest for me. You will probably see the 'Olympics' at the Asian Games this time because the strongest lifters in our weight category are from Asia," Mirabai said.The Indian's urgency was evident even immediately after her Glasgow victory. With the Commonwealth Games weightlifting hall dismantled, Mirabai, Sharma and physiotherapist Rohit Chhabria found a gymnasium and paid for a training session rather than lose valuable preparation time.Now, however, the Commonwealth Games are firmly behind her. The Asian Games are the sole target, with the longer-term picture involving a move up to the 53kg category for the Los Angeles Olympics."In Los Angeles, the weight class will be 53kg and I will need to bulk up. That should not be a problem, but everything will depend on the performance at Nagoya and then we can plan with the Olympic qualifiers in December," she said.Mirabai will spearhead a five-member Indian weightlifting contingent in Aichi-Nagoya and will be one of four women in the squad. The weightlifting competition is scheduled from September 22 to 28 at the Tokai Citizen Gymnasium.For now, though, there is only one destination in her mind — the Asian Games podium."It is mission Asian Games for me," Mirabai said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
