articles.title: B/R Trade Block Big Board Features Connor Hellebuyck, Dylan Larkin and Quinn Hughes for October 2026
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NHL regular season got underway earlier this week. As the long quest to the Stanley Cup playoffs begins, trade rumors continue to swirl among the pundits.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NHL regular season got underway earlier this week. As the long quest to the Stanley Cup playoffs begins, trade rumors continue to swirl among the pundits.

The trade market had been quiet since early July, with only two trades involving established NHL players. However, the Columbus Blue Jackets and Toronto Maple Leafs shook things up on Sept. 28, as the Blue Jackets sent winger Kirill Marchenko to the Maple Leafs for winger Matthew Knies in a six-player blockbuster .

That deal could result in more trade activity, especially if injuries strike or a team struggles through the opening weeks of the new season. Our October 2026 Trade Block Big Board has 15 players, some of whom appeared on our September Trade Targets Big Board .

Several new players have surfaced in media speculation. Others who featured on our previous board, like Vancouver Canucks center Elias Pettersson, Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Erik Karlsson, and Los Angeles Kings goalie Darcy Kuemper, were no longer topics of trade conjecture.

Follow along to see which players remain the subject of trade chatter and who the new trade candidates could be for October. Skills, experience, contract, and likelihood of being traded were factored into this compilation.

The Minnesota Wild were engaged in contract extension talks with Quinn Hughes during the offseason. With the 26-year-old superstar defenseman eligible for unrestricted free-agent status next summer, general manager Bill Guerin is understandably keen to get him signed before then.

Uncertainty about Hughes' future with the Wild generated speculation that he could be traded, perhaps to the New Jersey Devils to reunite with his brothers, Jack and Luke Hughes. That chatter landed him at No. 13 on our September Trade Targets Big Board .

Guerin addressed the ongoing negotiations with Hughes on Sept. 25. He said he's trying not to pressure the blueliner to sign, adding that it's a big decision for Hughes and his family. He intends to give Hughes all the time he needs.

For now, that should end the trade speculation that's swirled around Hughes since August. However, the longer he remains unsigned, the more his name could resurface in the rumor mill during this season.

The ongoing drama surrounding Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck has some observers wondering about the fate of other Jets stars, like Mark Scheifele, and their futures in Winnipeg.

On Sept. 24, Marc Dumont of Montreal Hockey Now cited Sportsnet's Nick Kypreos, who claimed the Montréal Canadiens were among several teams looking into Scheifele's availability. He noted that Kypreos believed the Jets would demand a high price for the 33-year-old center.

Scheifele is coming off a career-high 103-point performance last season. He's signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.5 million. The high-scoring center also has a full no-movement clause this season, and there's no indication he's willing to waive it or is asking for a trade.

The Jets are trying to find a suitable trade partner for Hellebuyck, but there's no indication they're peddling a core player like Scheifele, who is invaluable to their hopes of rebounding from last season's disappointing campaign. Nevertheless, his status could be worth watching, especially if the Jets struggle this season.

Before last season's March trade deadline, Jake DeBrusk raised eyebrows when he told reporters that playing for a rebuilding team wasn't something he would be willing to accept.

With the Canucks in the midst of rebuilding, the 29-year-old winger's remarks made him a fixture in the rumor mill.

DeBrusk is signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $5.5 million and a full no-movement clause. Nevertheless, he appeared in trade rumors throughout the spring and into the summer, making him a fixture on our NHL Trade Block Big Boards .

However, the conjecture surrounding DeBrusk faded as the summer went on. During a Sept. 9 interview with Sportsnet's Iain MacInytre, the winger indicated that he had quickly clarified his earlier comments, adding that he felt he could still help the Canucks and had never requested a trade.

Nevertheless, the rebuilding Canucks could be sellers again this season, especially if they struggle through the opening weeks of this season's schedule. That could make DeBrusk more open to a trade if a contender comes calling.

6 Players on Trade Watch After Marchenko-Knies Deal

The New York Rangers selected Alexis Lafrenière with the first overall pick in the 2020 NHL Draft. Over the last six seasons, they've waited patiently for the young winger to blossom into a scoring superstar. However, his inconsistency made him the subject of trade speculation in recent years.

As the retooling Rangers embark on the 2026-27 season, Lafrenière has resurfaced in the rumor mill. On Sept. 4, Ryan Lambert of The Hockey News included the 24-year-old winger on his list of players who could be traded if their clubs got off to a slow start.

The Fourth Period's Dave Pagnotta echoed that sentiment during a Sept. 22 appearance on Daily Faceoff's Morning Cuppa Hockey podcast. He felt Lafrenière could be among the high-profile Rangers who could appear in trade chatter if they stumbled through the opening weeks of this season.

Lafrenière is in the second season of a seven-year contract and lacks no-trade protection until 2027-28. However, his $7.5 million average annual value could be a sticking point if the Rangers were to peddle him, especially if his production remains inconsistent.

This season could be consequential for the Seattle Kraken. They made the playoffs once during their first five NHL seasons . Failing to qualify this season could lead to significant changes.

Jared McCann was among the players chosen by the Kraken in their 2021 expansion draft. Entering this season, he holds the team's single-season records with 40 goals and 70 points (2022-23) and is their all-time leader with 138 goals and 283 points.

On Sept. 4, Ryan Lambert of The Hockey News included McCann on his list of players who could be traded if their teams got off to a slow start this season. He speculated that the 30-year-old winger could be on the move if management decides to rebuild.

McCann is in the final season of his five-year contract with a cap hit of $5 million and a 10-team no-trade list. His ability to play center or wing and his scoring ability could draw plenty of interest from contenders if he becomes available in this season's trade market.

Earlier this summer, Boston Bruins general manager Don Sweeney said his goal was to re-sign Pavel Zacha . The 29-year-old center had a career-best 30-goal, 65-point season and is eligible to become an unrestricted free agent next July .

However, training camp opened without a new contract for Zacha. While Sweeney indicated that talks were ongoing with the center's agent, uncertainty about his future prompted us to examine six possible landing spots for Zacha if he becomes available before the March 1 trade deadline.

Zacha is in the final season of a four-year contract with a cap hit of $4.8 million. He also has an eight-team no-trade list. Another 30-goal, 65-point season could put him in line to earn $10 million annually on his next contract.

The Bruins will start this season with Zacha in the lineup. However, his name could surface again in the rumor mill if they struggle through October.

On Sept. 4, Ryan Lambert of The Hockey News included Ryan O'Reilly on his list of players who could be moved if their teams got off to slow starts this season. The 35-year-old two-way center is in the final season of his four-year contract with the Nashville Predators.

O'Reilly has enjoyed considerable success in his 17-season NHL career, taking home several individual awards and helping the St. Louis Blues win the Stanley Cup in 2019. He's entering the twilight of his career, but could still have value to contenders

We had O'Reilly on our list of pending free agents who could be traded this season , and players on bad teams who could help contenders . On Sept. 29, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that two league executives believe he'll be a player to watch in the trade market if the Predators don't re-sign him.

O'Reilly lacks a no-trade clause, but former Predators management treated him as though he had one. It remains to be seen whether new GM Chris MacFarland has the veteran center as part of his plans beyond this season. Nevertheless, O'Reilly could be worth keeping an eye on in the rumor mill.

Mason Lohrei surfaced in the rumor mill after the Boston Bruins were eliminated from the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs. The trade chatter carried on until July, making the 25-year-old defenseman a fixture on our NHL Trade Target Boards .

However, the rumors faded as the offseason continued. In August, Lohrei told The Boston Globe that he was focused on improving his game to remain a full-time roster player with the Bruins.

Lohrei was still with the Bruins when training camp opened last month, but the trade rumors had resurfaced. On Sept. 7, RG.org's James Murphy reported that multiple sources claimed the blueliner was again drawing interest in the trade market.

A restricted free agent with arbitration rights next summer , Lohrei could become a trade chip if he's no longer part of the Bruins' plans. His situation could be worth monitoring as this season progresses.

Reports claiming the Seattle Kraken were working with Shane Wright's agent to move the 22-year-old center had him on our August and September trade target boards. It seemed he would be with a new club when training camp opened in September.

However, training camp arrived with Wright still a member of the Kraken. Kate Shefte of The Seattle Times reported the club's high asking price and Wright's spotty NHL record hurt his value in this summer's trade market.

Wright was the fourth-overall pick in the 2022 draft. He seemed on the verge of a breakout performance after scoring 44 points in 79 games in 2024-25. However, his production and playing time declined last season under head coach Lane Lambert.

On Sept. 29, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Edmonton Oilers took a long look at Wright this summer but couldn't get a deal done. He's a restricted free agent next summer and might not fit into the Kraken's plans, which could keep his name in the rumor mill this season.

6. Samuel Montembeault, Montréal Canadiens

At the end of last season, it seemed that Samuel Montembeault had played his final games with the Montréal Canadiens. His struggles cost him the starter's job to Jakub Dobes, and then he lost the backup role to promising Jacob Fowler.

Montembeault was considered a trade candidate during the summer, but his poor 2025-26 campaign hurt his value to other clubs. Following a strong camp and preseason, the 29-year-old Montembeault remained with the Canadiens while Fowler was sent down to their AHL affiliate in Laval.

Nevertheless, trade speculation still dogged Montembeault during training camp. During a Sept. 17 appearance on The Jason Gregor Show , NHL insider Frank Seravalli boldly predicted the Canadiens goalie would be the first player traded this season.

Seravalli's prediction didn't pan out , but that doesn't mean Montembeault won't be moved this season. He's slated to become an unrestricted free agent next summer, and a strong performance could improve his value as a rental player in the trade market.

The Calgary Flames are continuing their rebuilding program as they enter this season. That's made Zach Whitecloud a frequent subject of trade rumors since the 29-year-old defenseman was acquired from the Vegas Golden Knights in January.

Sitting at No. 8 on our September NHL Trade Targets Big Board , Whitecloud's defensive skills and experience make him the Flames' most valuable trade chip. He's signed through 2027-28 with an affordable average annual value of $2.8 million and lacks no-trade protection.

On Sept. 4, Ryan Lambert of The Hockey News included Whitecloud on his list of players who could be moved if their teams struggle early this season. He would certainly draw attention from contenders looking for shutdown defensemen with Stanley Cup experience.

Whitecloud remains invaluable for the Flames as a mentor for promising defensemen like Zayne Parekh and Simon Nemec. Nevertheless, we can't dismiss the possibility of a contender making a big early pitch if the Flames stumble through October.

Emerging from a four-year rebuild, the Montréal Canadiens have several promising young players pushing for roster spots.

With forward Florian Xhekaj cracking the lineup in training camp, veteran forward Kirby Dach could be battling to retain his spot on the roster.

Dach, 25, was acquired from the Chicago Blackhawks during the 2022 draft. A big, skilled forward who can play center or wing, he's been hampered by injuries throughout his seven-season NHL career. Signed to a one-year contract , he faces an uncertain future in Montréal.

Writing for Casino.org, NHL insider Frank Seravalli stated that the Edmonton Oilers and Calgary Flames were interested in Dach. He claimed the Oilers' interest "bordered on drooling," pointing out that Edmonton general manager Stan Bowman drafted Dach in 2019 during his tenure as Chicago's GM.

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported the Oilers' interest in Dach stemmed from their lack of a right-shot center. However, the Canadiens could prefer to use Dach as a trade chip in a larger package offer for a scoring forward or right-shot defenseman.

3. Alexander Nikishin, Carolina Hurricanes

Defenseman Alexander Nikishin regularly appeared on our NHL Trade Boards since July, following reports that the Carolina Hurricanes were mulling over whether to trade or re-sign the 24-year-old restricted free agent.

It seemed unusual that the Hurricanes were considering moving a promising blueliner who lacked arbitration rights and was ineligible to sign an offer sheet. However, on Sept. 14, Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic reported that Nikishin had requested a trade.

Because of his RFA status, Nikishin missed training camp and preseason play as the Hurricanes attempted to move him. On Sept. 17, LeBrun wondered if the young defenseman might be part of a trade pitch to the Winnipeg Jets for Connor Hellebuyck.

However, on Sept. 25, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Nikishin wasn't interested in signing with the Jets. Friedman also reported that the New York Rangers and Hurricanes had the framework of a trade in place earlier this summer, but the Rangers and Nikishin could not agree on a contract.

For the second straight month , Dylan Larkin sits at No. 2 on our Trade Block Big Board. The 30-year-old center requested a trade during the off-season, but his narrow list of trade destinations and the Detroit Red Wings' ongoing search for a new general manager have hampered efforts to move him.

Larkin initially asked to be traded to the Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers, and Vegas Golden Knights. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported the veteran center expanded his list to eight teams. Friedman believes they included the Dallas Stars, Colorado Avalanche, Washington Capitals, and Tampa Bay Lightning.

The problem is that none of those clubs have the salary cap space to take on Larkin's $8.7 million average annual value through 2030-31. Most also lack suitable trade assets to meet the Red Wings' high asking price, as they reportedly sought Matt Boldy from the Wild.

Unless the Red Wings lower their price, it could take weeks, perhaps months, before they finally move Larkin. That means he could remain a prime trade candidate for the foreseeable future.

For the fourth straight month, Connor Hellebuyck tops our trade candidates .

The 33-year-old goaltender revealed in August that he requested a trade earlier in the offseason. He's currently suspended by the Winnipeg Jets for not reporting to training camp.

Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said the door is open for Hellebuyck to return. However, he also said he would keep searching for a trade that would benefit both sides. On Sept. 17, Paul Friesen of The Winnipeg Sun reported that Cheveldayoff wants a return that provides immediate help for the Jets.

On Sept. 8, The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported that the Carolina Hurricanes, Buffalo Sabres, and Utah Mammoth were among possible trade destinations. Two days later, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said he'd heard mixed messages about the New Jersey Devils, but James Nichols of New Jersey Hockey Now was skeptical .

Friedman reported on Sept. 23 that he'd heard the San Jose Sharks had "kicked tires" with the Jets. So far, however, it doesn't appear that they're working on a potential deal for Hellebuyck.

Cheveldayoff has a well-earned reputation for patience and driving hard bargains in trade talks, so this situation could take a while to resolve. Hellebuyck's contract could also be a stumbling block. He's signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.7 million and a full no-movement clause.

Stats via NHL.com . Contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Ranking the Top 10 Moments of WWE's Triple H Era
articles.summary: Triple H assuming creative control of WWE starting in the summer of 2022 marked a monumental shift for not only the company but also for the entire pro wrestling landscape.
articles.body:
Triple H assuming creative control of WWE starting in the summer of 2022 marked a monumental shift for not only the company but also for the entire pro wrestling landscape.

The transition of power from Vince McMahon and the drastic changes that came with it were apparent on screen almost immediately. Several recently released Superstars were brought back, others had their original ring names restored, and the overall vibe on the weekly programming was way more in line with what fans wanted to see.

Although the booking has been inconsistent for the better part of the past two years, some of the highest of highs in WWE history have happened during the Triple H regime. The powers that be have proved that when they're locked in and have their priorities in order, they're capable of delivering must-see television.

The follow-up hasn't always been ideal, but certain milestones from the last four years have stood the test of time because of their flawless execution and how well they were received.

These are the top 10 best moments of WWE's Triple H era.

The Road to WrestleMania 40 largely revolved around Cody Rhodes needing to "finish his story," and as grand of a culmination as the story had at the event itself, often forgotten is Rhodes' brutal—and bloody—encounter with The Rock on the penultimate Raw before 'Mania.

The Rock, making an unannounced appearance on the program, unleashed an all-out assault on The American Nightmare backstage before brawling with him to the outside of the arena and forcing him to bleed.

It was an outstanding visual that made Rhodes look like that much more like a babyface in peril heading into the biggest bout of his career.

Dominik Mysterio Betrays Rhea Ripley (SummerSlam 2024)

Dominik Mysterio's two-year pairing with Rhea Ripley played a pivotal role in him finding his footing as a heel with their weekly interactions and shenanigans being a recurring highlight on Raw between 2022 and 2024.

During Ripley's absence due to injury, the writing was on the wall, especially once Liv Morgan started scouting Mysterio and trying to drive a wedge between the two.

Although it could be seen coming from a mile away, Mysterio costing Ripley her Women's World Championship clash against Morgan at SummerSlam still packed a punch because of how long they had been together.

Solo Sikoa Joins The Bloodline (Clash at the Castle 2022)

All signs pointed to Drew McIntyre being the one to ultimately dethrone Roman Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship at Clash at the Castle 2022, and with McIntyre having a (somewhat) home-field advantage in the UK, the moment would have been nothing short of sensational.

The Scot was mere moments away from becoming champ in Cardiff, Wales, when Solo Sikoa emerged at ringside to aid Reigns to victory.

It was the biggest possible debut Sikoa could have had on the main roster, and it served as an epic introduction for him as the newest member of The Bloodline.

The Wyatt Sicks Arrive (Raw, June 17, 2024)

Fewer debuts in the Triple H era of WWE have made as big an impact as The Wyatt Sicks, whose arrival on Raw in June 2024 was wildly different than anything fans had ever seen before.

It followed months of cryptic teases on social media and on Raw, with everything paying a touching tribute to the late Bray Wyatt.

The Wyatt Sicks left a trail of destruction on the night of their first-ever appearance as a group on Raw, including an incapacitated Chad Gable. They were never able to match that mystique in the remainder of their run, but their debut will surely never be forgotten.

Damian Priest Wins World Heavyweight Championship (WrestleMania 40: Night 2)

The Judgment Day formed in the final months of Vince McMahon's reign, but it was Triple H who saved the stable from obscurity.

To this day, the group is still a staple of Raw, but its biggest moment together came when Damian Priest successfully cashed in his Money in the Bank briefcase to capture the World Heavyweight Championship.

It occurred in the immediate aftermath of Drew McIntyre's world heavyweight title win over Seth Rollins, which was thwarted by CM Punk. That paved the way for Priest to steal the belt, cementing his status as a main event player in the process.

Vince McMahon announced his "retirement" from WWE on July 22, 2022, and only three days later, Triple H was revealed as the new head of the creative direction.

With such a seismic shift happening so close to SummerSlam, it was unclear how quickly the change in leadership would take effect on television, though fans were optimistic it would happen sooner rather than later.

Sure enough, Triple H wasted no time in establishing that his regime would be an improvement over the one that preceded it by debuting Damage CTRL at the start of SummerSlam, a stable consisting of Bayley, Dakota Kai and Iyo Sky.

Bayley was returning from a one-year injury layoff while Sky was called up from NXT, and Kai was brought back to the company after being fired a few months prior. Women's factions weren't commonplace at that time in WWE, so the introduction of Damage CTRL was a sign that a new era had indeed arrived.

The group never lived up to its full potential as a result of subpar booking, but its shocking SummerSlam arrival gave fans a reason to be excited for the future.

9. Oba Femi Beats The Beast (WrestleMania 42: Night 2)

With Oba Femi being such a promising prospect during his dominant run in NXT, it was imperative that WWE booked him like a megastar once he arrived on the main roster.

His first main roster match being against Cody Rhodes on the night of John Cena's swan song from the squared circle was an encouraging sign, followed by the strong showing he had in the men's Royal Rumble match.

It wasn't until his WrestleMania 42 contest with Brock Lesnar was made official, however, that it became clear that he was destined for an elite level of superstardom.

The build to their bout was perfectly handled and made Femi look not only like an equal to Lesnar but superior with the way he left him laying on multiple occasions. There was no telling whether WWE would follow through accordingly, but in the end, they did have him go over when it mattered most.

The match itself was nothing special, yet it was exactly what it needed to be with Femi defeating Lesnar in decisive fashion as the crowd roared in approval. The Ruler was a made man from that point forward.

8. Paul Heyman and Seth Rollins Join Forces (WrestleMania 41: Night 1)

Roman Reigns and Paul Heyman were practically inseparable for nearly five years, even well after both were out of The Bloodline.

Going into WrestleMania 41, Heyman was still firmly in the corner of Reigns, but he was also associated with CM Punk stemming from a "favor" Heyman owed his former charge.

Heyman was the focal point of the buildup for their Triple Threat match with Seth Rollins at the event with the implication being that his managerial services were at stake.

The unadulterated animosity between Punk, Reigns and Rollins was on full display during their matchup. The climax of the contest came when Heyman delivered a vicious low blow to Punk, and just as it appeared he was going to help Reigns beat Rollins, he betrayed The Tribal Chief with another low blow as well.

Rollins' reaction revealed that he and Heyman were in cahoots, indicating that Heyman only helped him win because he saw him as his new cash cow. Saving such a huge twist in Reigns and Heyman's five-year arc for WrestleMania made the moment even bigger.

The concept of Rollins and Heyman leading The Vision coming out of The Show of Shows had plenty of potential, but a variety of factors caused the stable to fall apart sooner than it should have.

7. Seth Rollins' Heist of the Summer (SummerSlam 2025: Night 1)

While The Vision didn't revitalize Raw the way fans initially hoped, that didn't stop WWE from prominently featuring Seth Rollins at the forefront of the flagship show in the months that followed.

Rollins made enemies out of CM Punk, Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn and others but still managed to win the men's Money in the Bank ladder match for the second time in his career.

Before he could even tease cashing in the contract, though, he was injured in a Saturday Night's Main Event outing against LA Knight—or so it seemed.

To Rollins' credit, it looked legitimate, but online reports that surfaced soon afterward all but confirmed it was a part of a storyline. The Visionary abruptly disappearing from Raw fueled the speculation that it could be real, but there was also the possibility of WWE pulling off the swerve of the century.

Moments removed from CM Punk besting Gunther for the World Heavyweight Championship at SummerSlam, Rollins walked onto the stage with his crutches, only to dramatically drop them and walk to the ring completely healthy.

Punk fought valiantly but couldn't survive the signature Curb Stomp, leading to Rollins having his hand raised as the new world heavyweight champion. It wasn't quite his cash-in from WrestleMania 31, but it did serve as an innovative homage that electrified the audience all the same.

6. Bray Wyatt Returns (Extreme Rules 2022)

In Vince McMahon's final years in charge of WWE, many competitors were released after never being given a chance to show what they could do.

Some journeyed to other promotions while a select few remained free agents, which allowed them to be brought back once Triple H took over.

Chief among them was Bray Wyatt, who was unceremoniously let go in the summer of 2021. Various Easter eggs that aired on WWE TV in the fall of 2022 heavily hinted at Wyatt's return and created genuine buzz online.

The "White Rabbit" campaign gradually picked up steam heading into Extreme Rules, a show that closed with Wyatt reemerging from the darkness with the help of his friends from The Firefly Fun House.

For as excessive as WWE can be on the production side of things and not letting moments breathe organically, everything about the execution of this return was phenomenal. Not only was Wyatt welcomed back with open arms from the audience, the company was finally behind him and his creative genius.

The Eater of Worlds' return run was cut short when he tragically passed away less than a year later, so the time he spent being back was invaluable.

5. Sami Zayn Betrays The Bloodline (Royal Rumble 2023)

Sami Zayn's role in The Bloodline would have very likely not evolved beyond being a cameo had Vince McMahon remained in control of the company's creative direction. His interactions with the group only picked up once the Triple H era got underway, at which point it was evident that there was an endgame in mind.

Solo Sikoa joining The Bloodline in September 2022 was a major development for the faction, but Zayn's entertaining antics were truly the highlight of The Bloodline during that period. He was a thorn in the side of the stable on and off for months, yet they refrained from kicking him to the curb because he was useful to them in certain situations.

By the Royal Rumble, Zayn had gotten fed up with The Bloodline's abuse and finally hit his breaking point. Following Roman Reigns' successful title defense against Zayn's former friend Kevin Owens, The Bloodline continued attacking Owens until Zayn stepped in and attempted to put an end to it.

When Reigns pushed Zayn aside, Zayn responded with an emphatic chair shot to his back, sending the crowd into a frenzy. It was the moment fans had long been waiting for and it didn't disappoint.

This was the angle that set the stage for the stellar main event between Zayn and Reigns over the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship in Zayn's native Montreal the subsequent month.

4. Sami Zayn and Kevin Owens Vanquish The Usos (WrestleMania 39: Night 1)

The only installment from Sami Zayn's saga with The Bloodline that was better than his betrayal of the group was his grand tag title win with Kevin Owens not long after at WrestleMania 39.

Zayn fell short of becoming champ at Elimination Chamber as expected, but the more appealing prize remained in reach: capturing the tag titles with his best friend in the main event of The Show of Shows.

It was an almost unfathomable scenario, but all of the pieces fell into place perfectly. The reunion of Zayn and Owens wasn't rushed in the slightest, and when it eventually happened, the audience rejoiced.

The Usos held the Undisputed WWE Tag Team Championship for nearly two years, breaking the previous longest-reigning record by over four months. They put down every tandem that challenged them for their coveted titles, but Zayn and Owens posed the biggest threat of them all because of everything they had gone through as opponents in the years prior.

Their WrestleMania match with The Usos was filled with excellent action, suspenseful nearfalls and exciting callbacks to previous story beats. It also marked the first time a tag title matchup had ever headlined WrestleMania.

Zayn and Owens can forever hang their hat on ending The Usos' historic reign and the magic that went into making that moment a reality.

3. CM Punk Returns (Survivor Series 2023)

Creatively, WWE was consistently at its most satisfying in the Triple H era in 2023, notably post-SummerSlam when there were several stories and Superstars carrying the product simultaneously.

CM Punk became a free agent in September following his departure from AEW, but the circumstances surrounding his exit made a WWE return far from certain.

Plus, the product was hot enough without him, leaving many to believe that a WWE return wasn't in the cards. Most fans knew there was a small chance of him showing up at Survivor Series in his hometown of Chicago but didn't think much of it because of how far-fetched it seemed.

As the event was about to go off the air and the babyfaces celebrated their WarGames triumph over The Judgment Day, "Cult of Personality" blared throughout the arena and the Chicago crowd came unglued.

To prove it wasn't some sort of prank, Punk walked out on stage, soaked in the deafening reaction and stared down the wrestlers in the ring as the screen faded to black.

If there was ever a moment in the modern era when hell had in fact frozen over in WWE, that was it. The surreal sight sent the message that nothing was out of the realm of possibility anymore under Triple H.

2. John Cena Turns Heel (Elimination Chamber 2025)

John Cena announcing his retirement from the ring over a year in advance gave WWE fans all of 2025 to look forward and built anticipation for who his final batch of matches would be with.

The idea of Cena competing in his final WrestleMania sold itself, but the company aimed to make his match at the event even more enticing by turning him heel beforehand.

Seeds were planted as early as the Royal Rumble press conference when he declared for the Elimination Chamber match without qualifying for it, but fans chalked it up to a tease for something that was never going to happen and nothing more.

Heel Cena didn't start to sink in for fans until he hit Cody Rhodes with a low blow after embracing him in a hug at Elimination Chamber. The nod of approval from The Rock in the corner of the ring confirmed it: Cena had made a deal with the devil.

The reaction from the live crowd in Toronto was sheer shock and disbelief. It turned to discomfort once Cena began blasting Rhodes with the Undisputed WWE Championship belt as Rock and rapper Travis Scott encouraged his heinous attack.

It was the greatest heel turn in WWE history, despite the heel run itself being arguably the biggest blunder of the Triple H regime to date.

1. Cody Rhodes Finishes the Story (WrestleMania 40: Night 2)

Triple H nearly ruined his run as WWE's head booker before it could really get going by having Cody Rhodes fail to dethrone Roman Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship in the main event of WrestleMania 39.

They almost went in a different direction entirely the following year when The Rock resurfaced and essentially stole Rhodes' WrestleMania 40 main event with Roman Reigns. The fan backlash to the abysmal move forced WWE's hand and resulted in Rhodes getting his rematch with Reigns instead.

Their WrestleMania 39 encounter was more of a technical masterpiece, but their war at WrestleMania 40 was all about tying up loose ends and wrapping up the Bloodline saga with the most awe-inspiring finale of all-time.

The interference from everyone in The Bloodline (including The Rock) combined with the cameos made for an instant classic that the crowd ate up every minute of. Reigns holding the gold for four years was worth it for all of the insanity that ensued that night.

Rhodes fulfilling his destiny by "finishing his story" as spectacularly as he did was the epitome of a WrestleMania moment, and remains the peak of the Triple H era with nothing else we've gotten since then coming close to topping it.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Kasparov: "Nos advirtieron de que nuestras vidas corrían peligro, pero no me detendré ni me esconderé"
articles.standfirst: El campeón del mundo de ajedrez reconoce que los servicios de seguridad de Lituania y Estados Unidos le avisaron a él y a su colaborador de que podían ir a por ellos
articles.summary: El campeón del mundo de ajedrez reconoce que los servicios de seguridad de Lituania y Estados Unidos le avisaron a él y a su colaborador de que podían matarle
articles.body: "los servicios de seguridad de Lituania y Estados Unidos nos advirtieron de que nuestras vidas corrían peligro y que debíamos tomar precauciones, lo cual hice y seguiré haciendo". Son las palabras de Gari Kasparov, publicadas en el boletín informativo The Next Move, que ratifican la información difundida por EL MUNDO por sobre los planes de una red vinculada a la inteligencia rusa para asesinar a opositores exiliados. El Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos divulgó que está llevando a cabo una acusación formal contra una red dependiente de los servicios de inteligencia rusos, que estaría planeando ataques fuera de Rusia contra destacados opositores a Vladimir Putin y su gobierno. Kasparov reconoce que a él y a su colaborador Ivan Tyutrinnos no les han dicho explícitamente que sus nombres aparecieran en la acusación contra esta red, pero sí que sus vidas corrían peligro. El gran maestro de los tableros entró en política en 2003 y en 2013 tuvo que abandonar Rusia por la cada vez mayor presión contra él por sus posiciones opositoras. En 2024 entró en la lista del Gobierno ruso de 'terroristas y extremistas'. Se le ha puesto en 'búsqueda internacional'. El hombre que se enfrentó al superordenador Deep Blue apunta que desde el momento en que se retiró del ajedrez para oponerse a Putin, siempre le han preguntado si no temía por su seguridad, más aún cuando su amigo y opositor Boris Nemtsov fue asesinado a sangre fría frente al Kremlin el 27 de febrero de 2015. Ahora, el aviso recibido por Estados Unidos afirma que "no puede considerarse una sorpresa, pero aun así resulta impactante". "No me detendré ni me esconderé, aunque creyera que pudiera hacerlo. Creo que la mejor defensa es un buen ataque. Mi familia y yo no estaremos realmente a salvo mientras Putin siga en el poder en Rusia", apunta Kasparov que se encuentra ahora en Estrasburgo para "ejercer presión a través del Tribunal Europeo de Derechos Humanos y crear mecanismos legales para liberar los fondos rusos congelados, especialmente en Bélgica".

articles.title: Sporting scandals that shook the world: Lance Armstrong, Hansie Cronje, 'Crashgate'
articles.summary: Manchester City are far from the first. The lure of glory and riches on the biggest stages have tempted plenty of other sports stars to break the rules.
articles.body:
Manchester City being found guilty of fuelling an era of glittering Premier League success via a network of sponsorship deals, found by an independent commission to be a "sham", has shaken the world of sport.

The lure of glory and riches on the biggest stages have tempted plenty of others to cheat.

BBC Sport looks back on nine more sporting scandals, stretching back more than a century.

Cancer survivor. Cycling legend. American hero. Cheat.

Lance Armstrong had spent years vehemently and aggressively insisting that he had won all seven of his Tour de France titles between 1999 and 2005 without the help of performance-enhancing drugs.

His story was remarkable. Aged 25, Armstrong had been diagnosed with testicular cancer, with doctors warning he was likely to die given the disease had spread to other parts of his body.

He not only survived, but returned to dominate top-level cycling. His Livestrong Foundation was wildly successful, selling millions of yellow wristbands to raise money to support fellow cancer sufferers.

However, as the evidence and former team-mates allegations against him stacked up, Armstrong was stripped of his Tour de France titles.

Armstong eventually confessed to cheating in a blockbuster interview with talk show host Oprah Winfrey.

"I made those decisions, they were my mistake and I'm here to say sorry," he said, adding that the culture in professional cycling made using drugs non-negotiable.

Armstrong says sorry for doping Published 18 January 2013

South Africa's golden boy undone by love of money

Hansie Cronje was the golden boy of South African sport.

Good looking and charming, he led the nation's cricket team with style and authority.

President Nelson Mandela singled out Cronje in 1996 for the "excellent manner" in which he captained the Proteas.

However, Cronje's love of money, combined with a fast-growing betting industry and the organised crime it attracted, proved his downfall.

Cronje entertained the offers of match-fixers, calling team meetings to discuss the possibility of throwing matches and sharing thousands of dollars in inducements.

Most infamously, Cronje contrived to lose a rain-affected Test against England in 2000.

With South Africa still in the midst of their first innings on the final day, Cronje convinced England counterpart Nasser Hussein that in the interest of sporting entertainment each side should forfeit an innings, producing a sudden run-chase and giving England a shot at victory.

Cronje was praised for his Corinthian spirit. In reality, he had been motivated by a bribe of £5,000 to ensure the match did not end in a draw.

Cronje was undone when an Indian police wiretap of a bookmaker caught him in discussions about fixing matches.

Cronje confessed in early 2000, was banned from cricket for life and died in a plane crash two years later at the age of 32.

Hansie Cronje, match-fixing and plane crash that left a complex legacy

There was something particular about turn 17 of the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

In 2008, before the inaugural Singapore Grand Prix was held at the circuit, Renault driver Nelson Piquet Jr knew it did not have any overhead cranes to lift a damaged car from the track. There were no side entrances to allow a stranded driver to be pushed out of danger's way by marshalls either.

On lap 14 Piquet found himself in exactly in that unfortunate position. And, despite his initial claim that he had made a "simple mistake", the Brazilian had put himself there deliberately.

When Renault dropped him in 2009, Piquet Jr revealed that he steered himself into a concrete wall to crash his car. The safety car was deployed as officials cleared debris off the track.

Crucially, Piquet Jr's team-mate Fernando Alonso was the only frontrunner to have stopped for fuel and new tyres at the point of the crash.

As Alonso's rivals went into the pits, the Spaniard, benefitting from the reduced gaps caused by the safety car, moved up the field and went on to win the race.

While Alonso was cleared of any wrongdoing or knowledge of the plot, Renault team principal Flavio Briatore and chief technical officer Pat Symonds were banned from F1 for several years.

Still in F1 10 years after 'crashgate' Published 12 September 2018

Under the cover of darkness - the Premier League fix

Frank Lampard wheeled away in celebration after his well-hit shot from the edge of the penalty area beat Kevin Miller in the Crystal Palace goal in the 65th minute of a Monday evening Premier League game in November 1997.

As he was mobbed by team-mates, Upton Park was plunged into darkness.

The following month similar happened at Selhurst Park. Thirteen seconds into the second half - with Wimbledon and Arsenal goalless - the lights went off. The Christmas lights in nearby Croydon were raised as a possible cause.

An Asian betting syndicate had pulled the plug, using a remote control circuit breaker, to get each match abandoned at a scoreline which would maximise their profits.

The gang were foiled in their attempts to pull the deception for a third time. They had bribed a security guard at Charlton Athletic to allow them to plant a device at The Valley before Liverpool's visit in February.

However, a suspicious member of staff at the club tipped off police.

Four men were given sentences of between 18 months and four years for their involvement.

No expense was spared for the Winter Olympics in Sochi in 2014.

With a budget of $50bn (£38bn) - more than 25 times Vancouver's 2010 Winter Olympics spend - organisers created two entirely new resorts, bristling with security and military personnel.

But building facilities from scratch also gave the Russian hosts a chance to design an elaborate way around anti-doping measures.

A secret tunnel allowed a Russian secret service agent, disguised as a sewer engineer, to swap out his compatriots' urine samples, which contained traces of banned substances.

A special method had been developed to remove the tamperproof lids of sample bottles, which were then refilled with 'clean' urine that had been frozen before Russian athletes began doping programmes.

Forty-three Russian athletes were banned for life, 28 of whom successfully appealed against the full extent of their punishment.

Russia was banned from competing at the following Winter Olympics in South Korea, although athletes who could demonstrate their clean record were permitted to compete under a neutral flag.

Russia banned from 2018 Winter Olympics Published 5 December 2017

A camera crew caught the aftermath of the attack on Nancy Kerrigan in January 1994.

The 24-year-old figure skater was captured clutching her leg and repeatedly wailing "why?".

Kerrigan had been training at a rink in Detroit before the American national championships. As she stepped off the ice, a man rushed towards her and struck her on the leg with a telescopic baton.

The bodyguard and ex-husband of Kerrigan's rival Tonya Harding had hired a man to break Kerrigan's leg. They hoped to rule her out of the forthcoming Winter Olympics in Lillehammer, boosting Harding's chances.

It didn't work. Kerrigan recovered from heavy bruising in time to make the USA team, alongside Harding.

Amid a media frenzy, Harding, struggling with a broken lace on her boot, finished eighth in the Olympic final.

The competition broke viewing records in the US.

Harding was banned for life from the sport after admitting attempting to conceal the identity of Kerrigan's assailant after the attack.

Harding's ex-husband Jeff Gillooly, the attacker he hired and a getaway driver all spent time in prison for their part in the crime.

When Olympic figure skating met whodunnit

The headline written in the Chicago Daily News summed up the disbelief of a city, a nation and a sport when it emerged that superstar Joe Jackson and seven of his Chicago White Sox team-mates had apparently taken bribes to lose the 1919 World Series, baseball's biggest game.

First baseman Chick Gandil was the ringleader, while star pitcher Eddie Cicotte was the key figure.

A fee of $100,000 - worth about $1.6m today - was agreed with the head of a betting syndicate, with the money to be shared among the eight conspirators.

Cicotte's pitch, deliberately hitting Maurice Rath on the back, was a sign to his team-mates, and gamblers in the know, that the fix was on.

After the White Sox lost the series 5-3 to the Cincinnati Reds, the White Sox's suspicious owner Charles Comiskey sent word that the players needed to collect their pay cheques from him in person.

None of the eight fixers did. They left the stadium without their money. Rumours spread, followed by an investigation, and soon the players were in the dock.

Although a criminal court failed to convict the players, they were banned from Major League Baseball for life.

Jackson insisted until his death in 1951 that he was not involved and that, despite receiving $5,000, he had been deceived into signing a confession.

The data revolutionary who exposed baseball's big fix

At half-time in their first match at the 2000 Paralympics the coach of Spain's intellectual disability basketball team told them to stop scoring so quickly and let their opponents shoot more.

He knew the vast majority of the team were there under false pretences.

Of the 12 players in the squad, 10 had no intellectual impairment at all, but were keen amateur players who had been recruited months before the Sydney Games to supplement the team.

Spain, perhaps unsurprisingly, won gold convincingly, beating Russia 87-63 in the final.

The scam unravelled because one of the ringers was also a journalist.

Realising he was in the midst of an incredible scoop, Carlos Ribagorda played in Sydney and then published an article detailing the scandal on his return.

The team were stripped of their medals and the incident led to a total ban on athletes with an intellectual disability from the 2004 and 2008 Paralympics, destroying the careers of thousands of sportspeople around the world.

Fake Paralympians boss: 'I didn't know about cheating'

When public prosecutors tapped telephone calls at Italian football giants Juventus in 2004, they were hunting for evidence of doping.

What they believed they found was corruption on a far more systematic scale.

They thought they had evidence of Juve general manager Luciano Moggi pressurising referee officials to favour certain clubs, including his own. Moggi denied the claims.

However, Juve, AC Milan, Fiorentina, Lazio and Reggina were all implicated in influencing referees.

All were given points deductions, but only Juventus ultimately dropped into the second tier of Italian football.

There was a split in the club's superstar squad.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Patrick Vieira joined rivals Inter Milan for a combined £23m, Fabio Cannavaro and Emerson went to Real Madrid for £13.7m, Lilian Thuram and Gianluca Zambrotta joined Barcelona for £13m, and Adrian Mutu went to Fiorentina for £5.5m.

But other key players – notably Gianluigi Buffon, Alessandro del Piero, Giorgio Chiellini, Pavel Nedved and David Trezeguet – remained with Juve in Serie B.

Despite beginning the season with a nine-point penalty and an opening-day draw with minnows Rimini, Juventus were promoted at the first attempt.

The club still lay claim to the 2004–05 and 2005–06 titles that were stripped from them, counting 38 rather than the official 36.

articles.body: Hull City have been hit by another road accident involving one of their players near the club’s training ground. Lucas Gourna-Douath reportedly overturned his car on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham today.The incident comes only weeks after teammate Sorba Thomas flipped his Land Rover Defender on the same residential road. Thomas escaped the crash without injuries. Gourna-Douath’s accident also ended without anyone being hurt, according to Humberside Police, although the circumstances of the latest collision have not been confirmed.Lucas Gourna-Douath car crash comes weeks after Sorba Thomas incidentEmergency services were called to Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham following reports of a single-vehicle road traffic collision.Images from the scene showed a Mercedes lying on its side on the residential road. Two police officers could also be seen near the overturned vehicle.Humberside Police later confirmed that nobody was injured in the crash.The force said, “Officers and emergency services were called to reports of a single vehicle road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am this morning (Thursday, 1 October 2026). Thankfully, no one was injured as a result of the collision.”The accident reportedly involved Hull City midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath. The French player joined the club during the summer transfer window in a deal reported to be worth £10.5 million ($13.8m).The location has now attracted attention because it is the same stretch of road where another Hull City player was involved in a serious-looking crash just weeks earlier.Sorba Thomas overturned his £60,000 ($80K) Land Rover Defender on Millhouse Woods Lane. The vehicle ended up on its side after the accident, with pictures from the scene showing damage to the car and broken glass on the road.Thomas, who joined Hull City on deadline day, escaped the incident without injury.At the time, Hull City released a statement confirming the winger was safe.The club said, “Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club’s Cottingham training ground. articles.title: Backstage WWE and AEW Rumors on The Bloodline, United Empire and Mason Rook
articles.summary: The wrestling rumor mill continues to churn out reports on top stars across both WWE and All Elite Wrestling, including The Bloodline and its role at Money in the Bank—if it has one at all.
articles.body:
The wrestling rumor mill continues to churn out reports on top stars across both WWE and All Elite Wrestling, including The Bloodline and its role at Money in the Bank—if it has one at all.

Dive deeper into the latest on The Usos and Jacob Fatu, AEW's introduction of United Empire, and an update on NXT star Mason Rook in this collection of reports from top industry insiders.

In recent weeks, Solo Sikoa and Jacob Fatu have been abducted or taken out by the 946.

WrestleVotes provided an update as to why that has been the case creatively, reporting on WrestleVotes Live for Fightful Select that this is being done to explain their absence at Money in the Bank in New Orleans.

They noted that the goal is to give Roman Reigns no backup for his match with LA Knight so they can settle that rivalry definitively. The report also suggests The Usos could be next to be written off as the premium live event approaches on October 10.

A key theme of The OTC's world heavyweight title reign has been his ability to retain the championship cleanly, a contrast with the interference-heavy defenses of his previous run.

Reigns won the title from CM Punk on his own and has since successfully defended it against Fatu, Seth Rollins and Penta in great matches and without any help.

Considering Knight's point of contention with Reigns is how his family helped The Tribal Chief beat him in their first meeting, it makes sense that the intent here would be to take the possibility of Bloodline interference off the table, all while continuing to tell the WarGames-ready rivalry between the family and the 946.

How Can Will Ospreay Use United Empire in AEW?

According to Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select, Will Ospreay has been permitted to use the United Empire name because New Japan Pro-Wrestling does not own it, unlike the Bullet Club name.

Sapp wrote: "Sources that Fightful spoke to pointed to the fact that Ospreay himself trademarked the name in April of this year with the help of Michael Dockins. There were a number of sources familiar with the situation who confirmed Ospreay does own the name and has the freedom to use it however he wants."

Ospreay has introduced his own version of the group to AEW, with members including Andrade El Idolo, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, and The Brawling Birds' Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter.

Given United Empire's importance to Ospreay's career, its continuation in AEW is a fitting development for the new AEW world champion. It also gives him allies amid AEW's faction-heavy landscape, which includes The Death Riders, The Elite and The Don Callis Family.

Byan Alvarez reported on Wrestling Observer Live that few people know what is going on with Mason Rook and that the popular NXT star may be out of action for a while.

NXT's social media account reported on Tuesday that Rook was not medically cleared to compete.

The Englishman responded to the announcement on his own social media:

The 29-year-old was headed toward a showdown with Grayson Waller over the NXT Championship based on recent creative, so his sudden absence is a huge blow for the performer and the brand itself.

Rook's long-term health should take priority, and the situation will be worth monitoring as WWE provides further updates.

articles.title: Carlos Queiroz quits as Ghana coach after AFCON qualifying defeats
articles.summary: The Portuguese oversaw two defeats in the qualifying round for AFCON 2027 since taking the job again on September 2.
articles.body:
Carlos Queiroz has left his job as Ghana coach after a damaging defeat to Gambia in the qualifying round for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON ) 2027 deepened the Black Stars’ latest crisis.

The Ghana Football Association said on Thursday it had mutually agreed with the veteran Portuguese coach to terminate his contract, barely a month after reappointing him for a new mandate.

“This was not an easy decision, but both parties agreed that, under the present circumstances, ending our professional relationship was the most appropriate course of action, with the interests of Ghana, the Black Stars and Ghanaian football above everything else,” Queiroz said in a parting message published on the association’s website.

He added that “the necessary conditions were not fully established, and our recent performance added to the decision to bring this journey to an end”.

The decision followed Ghana’s 4-2 home defeat to Gambia in an AFCON qualifying match, a result made more painful by the four-time African champions surrendering a 2-0 lead at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Ernest Nuamah and Felix Afena-Gyan had put Ghana in control before Gambia struck four times to complete a remarkable turnaround. Ghana, having already lost 2-0 away to Ivory Coast , are now bottom of Group C without a point after two matches.

Queiroz leaves with a poor record of one win, two draws and four defeats in seven matches, with Ghana scoring five goals and conceding 10.

His departure ends a turbulent five-month association that began in April, when the 73-year-old signed a four-month contract to take Ghana to the 2026 World Cup.

Queiroz guided Ghana into the World Cup knockout stage for the first time since 2010, after beating Panama and holding England to a draw.

Colombia eliminated the Black Stars 1-0 in the round of 32.

His initial mandate ended after the tournament, but the GFA reappointed him on September 2 .

Queiroz’s exit leaves the GFA searching again for stability at a difficult moment.

Ghana sit six points behind Ivory Coast and Gambia after two matches, and with only the top two teams from each four-team group qualifying, the Black Stars already face an uphill challenge to avoid missing a second successive AFCON.

articles.title: Roger Federer’s foundation has helped expand early education across Southern Africa; in 2025, one South African initiative alone reached 300,000 children
articles.summary: Roger Federer’s legacy is no longer limited to tennis courts, Grand Slam trophies and records.
articles.body: Roger Federer’s legacy is no longer limited to tennis courts, Grand Slam trophies and records. Through the Roger Federer Foundation, the Swiss great has spent years helping children gain access to better early education. His work in Southern Africa has grown into a long-running effort involving schools, teachers, families, local organisations and communities.During a 2025 visit to South Africa, Federer highlighted the scale of that work, revealing that the Foundation had already provided quality preschool education to more than 300,000 children in the country. Yet his message was not simply about celebrating progress. He also pointed to the millions of children who still need better opportunities to learn and develop.Roger Federer’s foundation has made early education a long-term priorityFederer established his foundation in 2003 with a focus on improving educational opportunities for children. What began as a relatively small effort in South Africa gradually expanded into a broader programme across Southern Africa.By 2023, the Foundation said its work had already helped 2.5 million children gain better access to preschool education. Its programmes were operating in six Southern African countries, including South Africa, Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe, as well as Switzerland.The Foundation's approach goes beyond simply putting more children into classrooms. It also focuses on the quality of learning, teacher development and the support systems around young children. Its stated mission is to strengthen early and foundational learning systems so children have a chance to learn, grow and thrive.That focus is important because the first years of education can shape how children approach school later. A child who enters primary school with basic language, numeracy and social skills has a stronger starting point than one who has had little access to structured learning.Federer has repeatedly connected this work with the opportunities he received during his own childhood. Speaking during his 2025 South Africa visit, he said, “I worked tirelessly to achieve success in tennis.” He then linked that experience to his desire to give other children access to guidance and opportunity.More than 300,000 children have benefited in South AfricaThe most striking figure from Federer’s 2025 visit was the Foundation’s reach in South Africa.At a Johannesburg event, Federer said the organisation had provided quality preschool education to more than 300,000 children through its work in the country. ATP Tour reported the figure directly from his remarks, while BusinessTech also cited the same number when detailing the Foundation’s South African programmes.The figure needs some context. The available sources do not establish that a single programme reached all 300,000 children. Instead, the number reflects the Foundation’s broader work in South Africa. One of its notable programmes is the School Readiness Initiative, launched in 2019 to help vulnerable children make a stronger transition from Grade R into primary school.The initiative focuses on several areas that can make a difference in a young child’s early years. These include improving teacher skills, creating mentoring networks, involving parents and education officials, and giving schools better tools to monitor children's development.The programme also recognises that school readiness is about more than knowing letters and numbers. Children need support with language, social development, emotional skills and basic problem-solving before they enter the next stage of their education.BusinessTech reported that the Foundation had invested about R175 million in the School Readiness Initiative, with the programme designed to improve preschool participation, strengthen children's readiness for primary school and help reduce repetition and dropout rates.Federer says 1.3 million children still need supportFor Federer, the 300,000 figure is a milestone, but not an endpoint.During his February 2025 visit, he highlighted the gap that remains in South Africa. According to ATP Tour's report, Federer said another 1.3 million children were still waiting for better opportunities and basic learning resources, including books, playgrounds and building materials, as well as well-trained educators.That challenge puts the Foundation's work into a much wider context.South Africa has made efforts to expand early childhood development, but access and quality remain uneven. BusinessTech, citing UNICEF and South Africa's Department of Basic Education, reported that around 1.15 million children aged three to five were not enrolled in an early learning programme. It also noted concerns about teaching quality and educators' understanding of child development.Federer therefore used his visit to call for wider cooperation rather than presenting philanthropy as a complete solution. He met South African rugby captain Siya Kolisi, whose foundation also works with communities in the country, and encouraged business leaders to contribute to the effort.Reuters reported that Federer and Kolisi discussed the need for collaboration as South Africa faces continuing challenges in education. Federer also visited Salani Primary School in Mpumalanga, giving him an opportunity to see some of the Foundation-supported work more closely.The Foundation’s Southern Africa work stretches beyond South AfricaSouth Africa is only one part of Federer's education project.The Foundation has developed programmes across several Southern African countries, with an emphasis on helping children from vulnerable communities gain access to early learning. In Lesotho, for example, its School Readiness Initiative uses digital tools to help teachers access educational resources and improve classroom practice.The Foundation has also invested in teacher development. Its model recognises that giving children access to classrooms is only one part of the challenge. Teachers need training, useful resources and ongoing support if early education is going to produce lasting results.The organisation's wider work has grown considerably since its early projects in South Africa. In 2023, the Foundation marked its 20th anniversary, with ATP reporting that more than 2.5 million children had benefited from its education programmes by then.The Foundation's current resources also include the Early Learning Kiosk, a digital platform offering locally adapted tools and resources for quality pre-primary education.For Federer, the ambition now extends to ensuring that early education becomes available to every child who needs it. His 2025 South Africa visit showed that his post-tennis chapter is increasingly tied to that goal.The numbers tell part of the story. More than 300,000 children have already received quality preschool education through the Foundation's work in South Africa. Millions more have benefited from its programmes across Southern Africa and Switzerland.But Federer has made clear that the work is far from finished. The next challenge is reaching children who remain outside quality early learning and ensuring that those who do enter the system have trained educators, suitable resources and supportive communities around them.That makes the Foundation's work less about a single celebrity charity project and more about building stronger foundations for education. Federer may have finished competing professionally on the tennis court, but his long-term work in early education continues to focus on giving children the kind of start that can shape everything that comes after it.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Haas F1 Revenue Hits Record High ‘By Some Margin’ as Team Plots Major Growth
articles.summary: Haas has spent most of its Formula 1 existence as the sport’s budget operation, a team that ran lean rather than fast. But team principal Ayao Komatsu has co...
articles.body:
Haas has spent most of its Formula 1 existence as the sport's budget operation, a team that ran lean rather than fast. But team principal Ayao Komatsu has confirmed that his outfit is seeing record revenue.

Speaking with reporters in Madrid about the team's search for new commercial partners, Komatsu laid out just how much the financial picture has changed for him heading into next season.

The Revenue Numbers Komatsu Is Talking About

Asked directly about next year's budget and whether Haas might finally have room to lean into the sport's cost cap, Komatsu confirmed:

"For next year is a clear decent step up from this year so I'm very pleased about that one," he said. "But in terms of cost cap obviously it depends where we spend it, right? So the our revenue forecast is very good compared to this year, it's the highest we have had for history of Haas F1 team and then by some margin."

Komatsu was quick to separate revenue from spending, though. Having more money doesn't automatically mean Haas will push against the cost cap ceiling, since where that money actually gets allocated determines whether it even counts against the cap in the first place. "But whether we going to spend it within the area that is let's say counted as a budget cap or not is another matter," he explained. "So that's an internal thing but all I can say is we've done the budget part of a multi-year growth plan and then that's what we are committed to. So it's very good."

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 01: Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal of Haas F1 is interviewed during previews ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 01, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Joe Portlock/LAT Images)

Haas Wants to Stop Borrowing Ferrari 's Toolbox

The second part of the conversation got at something Haas watchers have grumbled about for years. The team has long run a patchwork operation, buying in components and technical support from Ferrari and Dallara as a satellite team rather than building everything in-house the way bigger-budget rivals do. A reporter asked whether the growth plan extends to infrastructure, given that fragmented setup.

"Whether you call it infrastructure or not but definitely a the part of the growth plan is to looking at how can we increase our capability and efficiency beyond what we have now," he said.

articles.title: Dropped Esteban Ocon defiant: Formula 1 is “where I belong”
articles.summary: Esteban Ocon says his departure from Haas isn't due to underperformance on his part – and that he's not looking for drives outside F1
articles.body:
This week the Haas Formula 1 team confirmed what had long been mooted in the paddock: Esteban Ocon will be leaving at the end of the current 2026 season. But the man himself has designs on staying in F1.

"My focus is on Formula 1," he said in Malaysia. "That is clear, that's where I belong, that's where I want to be. So I'm not going to look elsewhere.

"But you never know what can happen in Formula 1. As you guys know, things move every two seconds. So I'm still working on trying to find a solution for next year.

"For now, our focus is that and to do well on track. I think we've done pretty well in the last races and, for me, that's the best way to show that I still deserve to be in Formula 1.

"Of course, I need the car [to be competitive], which we didn't have for many, many races, including last year. So if we have that, it should work, as it did in Baku, as it did in Madrid. We'll see."

Ocon has had two up-and-down seasons at Haas after moving from Alpine , where he spent five years before falling out of favour with the latest management regime, headed by Flavio Briatore. He won the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix for Alpine from eighth on the grid, holding on tenaciously to track position he gained by threading through the first-corner carnage triggered by Valtteri Bottas .

His problem is that, to paraphrase the famous Henry Wadsworth poem There was a little girl , when Ocon is good, he's very good indeed – but when he's bad, the results are highly sub-optimal. At Haas he has struggled with a car riddled with inconsistencies, but team-mate Oliver Bearman has generally wrangled better results from the same machinery and invested less energy in complaining about them.

Oliver Bearman, Haas, Esteban Ocon, Haas

As an independent team, Haas is among the least well-funded on the grid, so it has often fallen behind over the course of a season through being unable to add significant performance through updates. Last year it got off to an unfortunate start when the VF-25 car suffered unexpected aerodynamic oscillations at high speeds, and was unable to run the low rear ride heights required to maximise 'ground effect'.

Ocon also complained regularly about instability under braking which came and went unexpectedly. After Friday practice in Abu Dhabi last year, for example, he told Canal+ he "felt like a rookie who's never driven an F1 car". But for the following days the issues absented themselves and Ocon qualified eighth, then raced to seventh.

"For the past 10 races we should have been performing like that," he said afterwards. "We clearly missed out on something. It leaves a bittersweet taste."

Missed opportunities have been a recurring theme throughout the 2026 season as the VF-26 has also been bedeviled by inconsistencies. At several races Ocon has alluded to the car performing differently, with measurable shifts in aerodynamic load, after routine strip/rebuild operations with the same components.

At Monza he chuckled in the media 'pen' post-qualifying when Motorsport.com suggested he should hire an exorcist.

But it's understood that the team began to feel Ocon wasn't taking enough responsibility for those occasions where he underperformed relative to his and the car's potential – even though Bearman has found his own car to be inconsistent. Ocon has a directness which can be interpreted as undiplomatic at best, combative at worst.

And yet it was precisely this quality for which he was hired.

"No, I don't think that has anything to do with that," said Ocon when asked if he was in effect being punished for the car's issues.

"I've just been doing my job trying to get the cars to where they should be. And at the end of the day, it has benefited everyone in the team because we see the result of the hard work that we've put in, and me pointing the fingers at the current issues.

"Obviously, I was the first one to experience that. So it took us a few races to realise that it was actually there. But we all realise since quite a while now that this has happened. And it's clear in everyone's mind, in the engineering office. So those are not the reasons."

The most likely candidate to replace Ocon at Haas is Rafael Camara – who, like Bearman, is a member of Ferrari's young-driver programme. He also brings some sponsorship, although this is understood to be a side benefit rather than the principal reason for bringing him aboard.

The only potentially vacant race seats for Ocon are at Cadillac, where both Sergio Perez and Bottas have options for next year which are yet to be taken up. There is also a possibility of taking a test driver role at Aston Martin with a view to moving up when former Alpine team-mate Fernando Alonso eventually hangs up his helmet.

"I'm not going to say I go here or there," said Ocon. "I keep working with the team, trying to do well, and I will assess the options later in the year.

"But as I told you guys, you know, everything can happen in Formula 1. And I want to be on the grid next year, for sure."
