articles.title: The SEC’s TV ratings dominance is getting scary for the Big Ten
articles.summary: Despite winning three straight national championships, the Big Ten faces a problem that’s entering crisis territory: the TV ratings gap between the Big Ten a...
articles.body:
Despite winning three straight national championships, the Big Ten faces a problem that's entering crisis territory: the TV ratings gap between the Big Ten and the SEC is widening.

Some of this can be dismissed by pointing to the soft schedule the Big Ten has opened with, how early we are in the season, or the fact that Ohio State vs. Michigan will, as always, juiced the conference numbers at the end of the season. But all that spin aside, it's a problem that is snowballing… and snowballing fast.

Worse yet, the Big Ten has nobody to blame for its growing problem but itself.

Under Kevin Warren's leadership, the Big Ten went down a path almost no other major pro league or college conference has navigated successfully: it cut business ties with ESPN and ABC.

The business case was there. The Big Ten would move forward with three other broadcast networks: Fox, CBS, and NBC. Plus, ESPN now controlled the exclusive rights to the ACC and the SEC, as well as half of the Big 12. How could the Big Ten even fit into a new reality in which ESPN and ABC had entered the honeymoon phase with the SEC?

Fox, through an arrangement that seemed to rankle sports media executives and is still not very understood by the average fan, owns and controls Big Ten media rights (as opposed to the conference itself owning the rights) and was more or less looking for renters for Big Ten rights it didn't want (games that would get dominated by SEC competition). All networks, including ESPN, were put through their paces, pitching Fox directly on why they should partner with the network for Big Ten inventory.

Ultimately, the Big Ten and ESPN divorce was finalized, a byproduct of ESPN's commitment to the SEC. Meanwhile, out of a desperate need for any marquee college football inventory, NBC and CBS signed on with Fox and the Big Ten. And here we are in Year 3 of our new college football world order.

So, a few years following their divorce from ESPN, how's it going for the Big Ten?

The ratings suggest things aren't going great .

Fox seems content with the current arrangement. They're making money, and the Big Ten has been largely happy cashing checks that are bigger than their SEC rivals by an average of around $400 million per year. Past feedback from fans and schools hasn't registered as a problem for Fox , as they have an effective blueprint for making money, which includes:

A mildly successful alternative to College GameDay

Enough mediocre games on BTN and FS1 to keep validating their cable carriage fees

Cashing checks from NBC and CBS for Big Ten games, the majority of which are pretty mid and get clobbered by SEC games … an arrangement those networks seem less than thrilled with .

It makes money. A handful of noon games do well. CBS and NBC usually have one or two games per year to puff their chests out about.

But in the larger picture, the Big Ten is fading, at least in terms of ratings and its television product. Obviously, three straight national titles have reset the discourse on the best conference on the field, but undeniable problems seem to continue unabated in the short term.

I've been told the conference itself has grown increasingly annoyed by the trend, as well as by Fox's de facto stance that the Big Ten needs to do more to help itself. There is a growing sense at the Big Ten, from those who work for the conference to the individual athletic departments, that, compensation aside, they are at a disadvantage when it comes to the television product. And they fear the situation is only getting worse.

Fox and the Big Ten Have a September Problem

From 2021-2023, Big Noon was the most-watched TV window in the sport. It's now fallen to a third behind ABC's primetime and 3:30 game, both around 8 million viewers per week, compared with Big Noon's 6.3 million weekly viewers in 2025. There's chatter that Fox's noon window could even end up behind ABC's noon game this season.

Fox's ability to compete with ABC's 3:30 and 7:30 time slots went out the window when Texas and Oklahoma moved to the SEC , and ESPN acquired the SEC game of the week, previously held by CBS.

Big Noon will have a handful of great games this year, and every year. But beyond that, the slot is often filled with duds. So far this season, Big Noon has opened with North Texas vs. Indiana, Oklahoma vs. Michigan, Kent State vs. Ohio State, Illinois vs. Ohio State, and Michigan vs. Minnesota.

None of these games featured two ranked teams. The spreads for three of those games were 27, 41, and 52. You can probably understand why Gus Johnson has seemingly been sulking .

Fox didn't even send Big Noon Kickoff to Kent State vs. Ohio State. Ultimately, they knew the size of the Ohio State fanbase might draw a bigger audience than their other options that day, even against a 50-point underdog, but they couldn't even sell their Saturday pregame show for that game.

Fox is ultimately prioritizing a TV ratings projection versus airing a competitive game. This strategy does help maximize viewers, but it significantly diminishes the Big Noon brand and seems to act as a Quaalude for Gus Johnson. While they squeeze out mediocre ratings by going to objectively crappy Ohio State, Michigan, and Indiana games over and over, the cost is that most fans now know Big Noon is only "big" a handful of times each season.

At the end of the day, it's hard to puff out your chest about having the best pregame show and best games when you're broadcasting uncompetitive afterthoughts more weeks than not.

ESPN/ABC Have Way More Games to Choose From than Fox

If you asked me what the best thing to happen to ESPN in 2026 has been, it would be that both the ACC and SEC moved from eight conference games to nine. The end result is eight more conference games for both leagues.

Now, the SEC's second-to-last weekend of the season is no longer a box of cupcakes. This also means both leagues have more conference games before October. At least a dozen blowout games with no national interest have been wiped out in favor of conference games, many of which have significant value to ESPN.

The Big Ten was already at nine games, and unfortunately, some of them feature TV-ratings kryptonite: Rutgers, Maryland , Purdue , and Northwestern, along with the sagging national interest in Minnesota, Wisconsin , Nebraska , and Michigan State. Penn State , reliably the conference's third TV-ratings workhorse, suffered a surprise loss this past weekend, made more noteworthy by the rare sight of large swaths of empty seats at Beaver Stadium.

Oregon and Indiana certainly deliver on the field for the Big Ten, but they don't deliver anywhere near the audience of Michigan and Penn State when those schools are winning (something that is very much in limbo). The competitiveness of each conference's slate of games isn't on equal footing and might get worse depending on how Michigan and Penn State trend.

The SEC is a more diversified television product than the Big Ten, which relies too heavily on Ohio State, Penn State, and Michigan to move the needle. When these teams fall out of the Top Ten, the Big Ten teams that may take their place just don't pull the same TV ratings. This is less of an issue for the SEC, where the bench of programs that can drive ratings when successful is significantly deeper. The SEC doesn't need certain programs to win to be successful.

Another disturbing trend for the Big Ten is that ESPN is starting to schedule better games at noon on ABC versus later in the day on ESPN and is doing so to purposefully chip into Fox's eroding position at noon.

"SEC All Day" Loyalty and Frictionless Viewing is Crushing the TV Nomad

A normal Saturday for SEC fans means waking up and choosing between two pregame shows: College GameDay or SEC Nation, both of which might be on-site on an SEC campus. Often, ESPN has what it has branded "SEC All Day," which gives you two, or even three, ranked-team matchups. From pregame show to bedtime, fans have to change the channel once (from ESPN to ABC). From there, it's familiar announcers, familiar teams, and familiar rivalries.

I believe the biggest reason for the SEC's television trajectory is loyalty to the conference and reduced friction in consuming the product. Fans no longer have to go to CBS in the middle of the day for the best game. The schedule is more potent than ever, with more conference games and fewer cupcakes, as Oklahoma and Texas further bolster the conference's blue-chip brands. Bars and restaurants are also helping the ratings trend, with more televisions set to ABC and left there until 11 p.m.

The SEC on ABC is the most dependable thing on television on Saturdays. There is no Kent State, North Texas, or Rutgers to worry about.

Now consider the Big Ten setup. Big Noon Kickoff was in London earlier this month for a non-Big Ten game. Before that, the show has spent most weekends on-site for mediocre or downright uninspiring contests. Dave Portnoy and the Barstool Sports partnership haven't delivered ratings the way Pat McAfee and his field-goal-kicking contest have for ESPN. Before any game has even kicked off on Saturday, the Big Ten is already behind, ratings-wise and on social media.

In weeks when Fox has a good noon game, and the Big Ten leads the SEC early in the day, that advantage almost always dissipates by 3:30. Some Big Ten fans flip over to CBS, but if there's a better game on ABC, conference loyalty goes out the window.

And that's often the case. The millions of fans watching Ohio State vs. Penn State at noon are not getting delivered to whatever game CBS is airing at 3:30 anywhere near the level at which SEC viewers simply roll into ABC's 3:30 game. USC vs. Rutgers at 3:30 on CBS is just not a game that has any drawing power. Most Big Ten fans are still questioning why either team is in the Big Ten.

The Big Ten's television setup is like when you're bar hopping: You lose people along the way.

Taking that analogy one step forward, SEC fans just drink more. They stay at the same bar (ABC) and drink longer. Fans of other conferences bar hop from channel to channel, but do it for fewer hours, and leave some friends behind along the way, many of whom end up at ABC.

To the untrained eye, this past Saturday's last-second Iowa win over Michigan and Oregon's heated win over USC would suggest the Big Ten fared well against the SEC.

This is what a good weekend looks like for the Big Ten right now.

This is what the ratings look like for a bad weekend of games.

It's not just the friction of following the conference; it's loyalty. Most college football fans watch their team, and if they watch other games, they often just pick the best one on at that time. When a game ends, Big Ten fans are released, and many of them reliably migrate to an SEC game. For SEC fans, that migration is clearly much less of a thing. They stay. The next game on ABC is often the best game on. Big Ten fans are forced to bar hop and often end up consuming huge amounts of SEC football too.

College football, and particularly the SEC, just looks better on ESPN. There are many, many reasons for this.

For starters, football looks better under the lights, when ESPN/ABC schedules its best games. Football games are louder at night, and the overall atmosphere surrounding ABC's primetime games reliably feels bigger.

Second, scorebugs are subjective, but I find the Fox college football scorebugs a step above locally broadcast high school games. Overall, Fox's graphics package seems well below ESPN, NBC, and CBS. They aren't as shiny, clean, or crisp. Even the folksy SEC theme music on ESPN has become an earworm after a few years.

Finally, ESPN invests far more time and energy into capturing the atmosphere before a game. Fox tends to show teams running onto the field, while ESPN shows the slow walk from the locker room through a tunnel and onto the field. There are more crowd shots. They also have impressive Brad Pitt-narrated opening videos. ESPN often has shots of people around campus and outside the stadium. They put a lot of production effort into transporting viewers to the venue so TV audiences feel like the fans in attendance. Fox does some of this, but it's less extensive and less consistent. SEC games consistently feel bigger, and that often is enough to bring in casual viewers with no skin in the game. Other conferences and networks don't consistently match the priority and commitment to ESPN showcasing the pageantry of SEC college football.

Depending on whether Fox is airing the Big Ten championship game (they did last year because NBC ominously chose not to air the Big Ten Championship ), their biggest game of the year is Ohio State vs. Michigan . By 4 p.m. on the last Saturday of November, Fox's influence and role in the sport are all but done.

Throughout the year, ESPN promotes and champions the SEC's superiority (recent results have muddied that narrative). The bias is definitely there . They don't like you pointing it out , but that argument has long been lost. But when you turn the page to December, Fox's Big Ten counterbalance to ESPN's pro-SEC viewpoint essentially vanishes from the sport.

GameDay 's competitor goes away. Joel Klatt disappears. At that point, the Big Ten relies entirely on a network it walked away from. Fox and their enlisted partners hurt the Big Ten by being irrelevant starting in December.

The most-watched games of the year take place in December and January, all of which air on ABC, ESPN, or TNT (which ESPN still produces). Christmas ad spending rolls in, as do huge CFP ratings. No wonder Fox is desperately trying to expand the playoff , so it can have a piece of the pie.

Is the Widening Gap a Problem? And What Can Be Done?

Setting the ratings aside, the Big Ten makes more TV money than the SEC. Others will point out that the Big Ten's footprint encompasses more people (good for cable carriage costs), and Big Ten viewers have higher annual incomes than SEC viewers on average, which is appealing to advertisers.

Those explanations help the suits sleep better at night.

As a Big Ten alum, I don't care if the Big Ten is second in terms of ratings. What I do care about is that the product is falling behind and the ratings gap is widening. I also care that its primary television partner doesn't seem to have answers or urgency about the situation because the current setup works fine for them. They generally view it as the Big Ten's problem for having a weaker schedule from top to bottom than the SEC.

ESPN and the SEC have been in a good marriage. It's elevated the product and conference at a time when the on-field results have actually dipped. The strategy is working. If you're a Big Ten fan or alum, you want the same type of marriage that the SEC has, not whatever this current arrangement is.

You can say the Big Ten's strategy is working. They are winning on the field when it counts and cashing bigger checks. But with a widening gap in interest, excitement, and product quality, I'm just not sold that either of those things will hold true in a decade.

articles.title: Rutgers Scarlet Knights Basketball 2026-27 Season Preview
articles.summary: Despite his recent cancer diagnosis, Steve Pikiell's Rutgers Scarlet Knights are preparing for his 11th season in Piscataway. His teams have always proven to...
articles.body:
Despite his recent cancer diagnosis, Steve Pikiell's Rutgers Scarlet Knights are preparing for his 11th season in Piscataway. His teams have always proven to be hard-nosed and tough, just like the fight Pikiell is going through himself.

While Pikiell's health and well-being are important, the Knights have to focus on the season. That's where Rutgers can lean on its experience, as it returns several key playmakers on the guard. Senior Tariq Francis leads that group.

With Francis at the forefront and some major transfer additions, the Rutgers Scarlet Knights look ready to fight for their coach this season. Let's take a closer look at the 2026-27 Scarlet Knights.

Rutgers Scarlet Knights Basketball 2026-27 Season Preview

As mentioned above, Francis returns. He had one heck of a season in 2025-26. He finished with an average of 17 points per game, and really developed a good bond with other guards like Leno Mark and Jamichael Davis .

In Davis' case, he's a two-time captain and by far the most experienced Rutgers player. He has been with Rutgers since the 2023-24 season. The Scarlet Knights had to do some real work in their frontcourt, however, as starting center Emmanuel Ogbole looked to try his hand at Kansas . Thus, Rutgers went to the portal and landed two bigs that will certainly shore up the post.

Those players are Dorin Buca , a 7-foot-2, 286-pound transfer from Kansas State. As well as Christian Gurdak from Virginia Tech. Both have some steps to take this season, but they both give Rutgers size and strength in the post.

Add in some other fresh faces like Mervedi Miteo from the Congo, along with a returning sophomore, Gevonte Ware , ready for a bigger role, and Rutgers has the size and depth to take it to others in a tough Big Ten . Time will tell what Kaden Powers can do in his second season as well, after breaking into the starting lineup last season.

Returners: Francis, Darren Buchanan Jr ., Mark, Max Fradkin , Ware, Powers, and Davis.

Newcomers: Buca, Darin Smith Jr ., Gurdak, Imahri Wooten , Miteo, RaSheed Jones , Will Sydnor , Martin Tonejc , and Diego Garavagila .

Rutgers does have a chance to live up to their coach's grit and toughness in this season's non-conference slate. It all starts with a pair of exhibition matchups with two of the most prominent programs in the New York and New Jersey area.

The Scarlet Knights face Villanova at Jersey Mike's Arena before traveling to Madison Square Garden to face Rick Pitino's St. John's Red Storm. The Knights face plenty of other local teams, with New Haven, NJIT, and Bryant all visiting Piscataway.

Things get really challenging beginning November 17; the Knights return to Las Vegas for the Players Era Festival. First on the schedule is the Houston Cougars. That's a massive first game, and the event doesn't get any easier with so many other top programs involved.

Rutgers is guaranteed two more games as part of the event. Jumping ahead to what will be a challenging Big Ten. Especially when they have to travel to Bloomington on December 1 to play the Indiana Hoosiers, followed quickly by a title game against the Defending National Champion Michigan. The Seton Hall Pirates are the final big foe of Rutgers' non-con schedule.

For the rest of the Big Ten slate. Rutgers will have a road clash at Purdue and a road trip to East Lansing in early February, where they nearly defeated Michigan State on Senior Night last season. Getting USC and UCLA both at the RAC is a huge draw, especially as Rutgers fights to get back amongst the top 15 of this 18-team league.

Given his health situation, it wouldn't be right to say that Pikiell could be on the hot seat this season. He's a good ball coach and has gotten Rutgers to the Big Dance in the past. This group looks like it has the pieces to give everyone they play a tough time.

You already saw it last year, when they had Michigan State on the ropes late in both meetings. Heck, they won a Big Ten Tournament game last season against Minnesota, which had a little bit better talent. Not to mention, they hung around with UCLA in the second half of their second-round game.

They got to taste post-season play last year as well, earning a Big Ten invite to the College Basketball Crown, which is a moot point now that the NCAA tournament field has been expanded. No matter the outcome for Rutgers basketball in 2026-27, they will go to war for Pikiell.

articles.title: 2026 Heisman Week Four Poll
articles.summary: Welcome to the 2026 Heisman Week Four poll. We welcome two new players to the poll, Kamario Taylor, the quarterback for Mississippi State. As well as Jadan B...
articles.body:
Welcome to the 2026 Heisman Week Four poll. We welcome two new players to the poll, Kamario Taylor, the quarterback for Mississippi State. As well as Jadan Baugh of Florida, who is coming off a stellar game against Ole Miss. As we enter week four of the season, the games keep getting bigger, and the stakes are getting higher. To see all the movement from last week, check out the Week Three poll . Again, a reminder that the Poll is weighted. The player gets five points for every first-place vote, four points for every second-place vote, three points for every third-place vote, and so on. Let's get to it: our Week Four Heisman Poll.

#5 Kamario Taylor, Quarterback, Mississippi State

Kamario Taylor is new to our Heisman poll. He has 1,192 yards and 14 passing touchdowns this season. Against Missouri, he threw 27 passes for 360 yards and three touchdowns. That last TD was a 24-yard game-winner with 3:57 left in the game to beat No. 19 Missouri. This is the Bulldogs' first top-25 win since Dak Prescott in 2014. The Bulldogs are currently ranked #16 and are 4-0. This weekend, they host the Crimson Tide. Should be a great game between two undefeated teams.

Next game: vs. Alabama, Saturday, October 3rd, 11:00 am CST

After Jadan Baugh's performance against Ole Miss, he was named the SEC Offensive Player of the Week as well as the Doak Walker National Running Back of the Week. Baugh had 29 carries, 142 yards, and three touchdowns. Baugh has rushed for over 100 yards in five straight games dating back to last season, holding status as one of three Gators to accomplish the feat all-time (Fred Taylor, Emmitt Smith). Florida had its highest-ranked win in over a decade against. Can they keep the momentum up when they travel to Columbia on Saturday?

Next game: at Missouri, Saturday, October 3rd, 2:30 pm CST

#3 Trinidad Chambliss, Quarterback, Ole Miss

Coming off the huge win over LSU, the Rebels got beat down in the swamp. In the Florida game, Trinidad Chambliss had 342 total yards and three touchdowns. The Ole Miss quarterback passed Eli Manning to take third place in a passing record that had stood since 2016. Chambliss has 1,222 yards and eight touchdowns this season. This weekend he and the Rebels travel to Nashville and take on Vanderbilt in hopes of bouncing back. A very cool moment captured after the game was a video of Chambliss waiting to congratulate Jon Sumrall. See tweet below.

Next game: at Vanderbilt, Saturday, October 10th, 2:30 pm CST

#2 Jeremiah Smith, Wide Receiver, Ohio State

After the Illinois game Jeremiah Smith was named Maxwell and Walter Camp National Player of the Week as well as being named player of the week by the AP and the Big Ten. He had 12 receptions, for 217 yards and four touchdowns. Bringing his season totals to 33 receptions for 617 yards and seven touchdowns. Smith is only four games into the season and the record books are being rewritten. This weekend Smith and the Buckeyes travel to Iowa City to take on the undefeated Hawkeyes.

Next game: at Iowa, Saturday, October 3rd, 2:30 pm CST

Darian Mensah continues to break records. The latest and greatest stat for Mr. Mensah is that he has more touchdown passes than incompletions through his first four games. Since 2004, the only quarterback besides Mensah to have more touchdowns than incompletions in the first three games was Baylor's Robert Griffin III in 2011, the year he won the Heisman Trophy. Last weekend, Mensah routed Central Michigan 52-3, where he threw for 338 yards and three touchdowns. This season, he has 1,211 yards, 14 touchdowns, and zero interceptions. This weekend, Mensah and the Hurricanes travel to Clemson for a cool, crisp fall night in Death Valley.

Next game: at Clemson, Saturday, October 3rd, 6:30 pm CST

The season marches on, and we're heading into week four. Big games this weekend it will be fun to see where everyone lands. Enjoy the games. Be sure to check back next week to see where your favorite player lands on our weekly Heisman Poll. Also, the Heisman Fan Favorite Vote is live. Vote for your favorite player.

articles.title: 'Just sports': Female athletes aren't buying Sydney Sweeney's Novig ad
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney's nude ad for Novig boosted the app's ranking but drew backlash from female athletes, including at FSU. Sweeney has not commented.
articles.body:
Sydney Sweeney overestimated her audience's appetite for baring all on-screen in a Sept. 9 advertisement for sports prediction market platform Novig. The campaign, beaming from Times Square billboards, pushed a "Just Sports" message female athletes saw as undermining the recognition women's teams have spent years fighting for.

The commercial features Sweeney posing nearly nude behind strategically placed sports equipment, then in pieces of athletic gear like football pads and a catcher's helmet. In the ad, Sweeney said , "Novig is just sports. So they wanted to show just sports." The ad drew backlash from critics, including female athletes, who said it objectifies women and diminishes their achievements in sports.

"As a company, we're hugely supportive of women's sports. I think it's a huge component of our platform … I think we never intended to portray female sports," Novig CEO Jacob Fortinsky said at a Front Office Sports event on Sept. 15. "Sydney's an actress, the biggest movie star in the world. We're a prediction market that is focused on sports. And that was the story she was communicating … It really was Sydney who's driving a lot of the visuals and the messaging."

The message was a hard sell for female athletes, considering no actual athletes appear on screen. Women in sports have faced long-standing scrutiny over how they compete and what they wear, with officials rebuking them for showing too much skin — or too little.

Gymnastics, track athletes, and beach handball players have been policed over leotards, briefs, and bikini bottoms, the athletic wear they need to perform well and comfortably.

After the ad's release, female athletes took to social media, saying it undercuts the fight women have waged over their own uniforms. Four-time Olympic swimming champion Ariarne Titmus asked how society could still be "monetizing a woman's body and sexualizing women's sport."

Former UCLA gymnast Gracie Kramer posted an Instagram reel of herself competing and training, captioned, "idk what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what a woman in sports looks like." Female athletes flooded social media with similar posts showing the time, dedication and effort they put into their sports.

"I think after all the work women go through to be respected in their sports and not sexualized as an athlete, it sets us back and puts the attention back on what we're trying to get away from," Mikayla Chavez, president of FSU's club cheerleading team, said to the FSView. "It just reinforces the idea that men only care about sex and sports and gives them a pass to look at her as an object."

What team is Sydney Sweeney playing for?

After the ad was released, Sweeney posted a series of covers from ESPN The Magazine's Body Issue. The special edition featured athletes posing nude or semi-nude, including Serena Williams and Ronda Rousey.

That same day, she told Complex that the ad was "a very simple and playful idea to "really bring the concept of 'just sports' to life."

But Sweeney is not an athlete. The Body Issue photos frame those athletes' strength; they're revealing, but not sexual. Williams' cover represented more than an ideal female body — she showed the dedication it takes to build a strong one.

"Being a female athlete shows that my body is meant for more than what a man wants it to be," Chavez said. "It's meant for movement, hard work, freedom and the strength to do anything a man can do."

The ad was built to reach as much of Novig's target audience as possible: men, who make up most of the sports betting market and probably aren't thinking about her autonomy while watching. While the ad may empower her, the industry weaponizes that sexuality for profit.

As an actress, Sweeney may be acting out of an understanding that her strengths as a performer are often overshadowed by her figure. While she trained to play boxer Christy Martin in "Christy," cruel comments flooded paparazzi bikini photos of her.

Sweeney responded the way she's doing now: she paired the hateful comments with a Rocky-esque training reel to show her dedication to her body and her work. The film went on to flop , opening to $1.3 million in November 2025. Afterward, she wrote on Instagram that "Christy has been the most impactful project of my life."

However, with Novig, it's hard to separate the ad's implication from its intended message. While she may feel empowered, prioritizing the male gaze for buzz isn't sitting right with some of Sweeney's fans.

"I think her ad is a complete flop," FSU media and communications major Grace Healy said to the FSView. "I think that she's exploiting herself and has nothing to do with women's sports. I think too many people are focused on sexualizing themselves and not necessarily what they're made of and what they can do."

Sweeney is not the first to understand that sex sells, and the ad accomplished exactly what it set out to do. However, it heightens concerns about the oversexualization of media. After Sweeney played one of the most famous female boxers of all time, it's surprising to see this shift of tone when she sports the uniform.

Novig climbed from No. 50 in August to No. 11 in the App Store's sports rankings, and its average weekly brand mentions jumped from 392 to 4,633 in the four days after launch, according to social listening firm Peak Metrics. However, only 4% of those posts mentioned the app itself.

The ad's virality shows the nudity was meant to draw audiences to the app. By tying sports betting to the rush of a nude figure, Novig reached the viewers it was after.

Beyond the backlash, the ad highlights competition in the prediction market, where Novig is trying to set itself apart from rivals like Kalshi and Polymarket. Novig's "no wars, deaths or politics" pitch is aimed squarely at them.

By turning attention to Sweeney and sports, Novig avoided any political affiliation and took a bold swing to promote the platform. But it struck out with its female audience and with sports as a whole, forgetting that sports include women's sports, too.

By ignoring the other half of the population's dedication to sports, Novig has pointed to the idea that sports are by men, for men, instead of a community everyone can enjoy.

A trio of former Denver Broncos players are set to face their old team on Sunday.

The San Francisco 49ers ' defense features starting inside linebacker Dre Greenlaw , who is backed up by Garret Wallow . Both linebackers played for the Broncos last season.

On special teams, the Niners have punter Corliss Waitman , who handled punting duties in Denver in 2022. San Francisco also has outside linebacker Andrew Farmer (on injured reserve) and running back Sincere McCormick (on the practice squad). Farmer spent most of the 2024 season on the Broncos ' practice squad. McCormick had a brief stint on Denver's practice squad last December.

The most notable ex-Bronco facing his old team is Greenlaw. The 29-year-old linebacker signed a three-year, $31.5 million contract with Denver in 2025, but missed nine games last fall (eight due to injury and one due to suspension ). The Broncos cut Greenlaw this spring in a move that saved about $8 million in salary cap space, opting instead to bring back Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad .

After being cut by Denver, Greenlaw returned to San Francisco, where he spent the first six years of his career. Greenlaw and the 49ers are now set to host the Broncos on Sunday afternoon.

"He was the OG in the locker room and the offense in my early years, really showed me what it was to be a great teammate. Somebody who just loved the game of football and loved the atmosphere of being a pro and living out your dreams." Said Kelce

articles.title: Seahawks plan to continue rotating at RG in Week 4
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks plan to continue rotating at RG without Anthony Bradford in Week 4.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks will once again be without starting right guard Anthony Bradford against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4. Bradford was placed on IR prior to the Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders . He'll miss the second of a minimum four-game absence due to IR rules.

The Seahawks deployed an interesting plan at right guard without Bradford in the lineup. Head coach Mike Macdonald chose to use both Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens at right guard versus the Commanders. The Seahawks essentially rotated them in/out on a drive-by-drive basis.

Coach Macdonald confirmed that will once again be the case in Week 4.

Haynes played a position-high 40 snaps at right guard in Week 3. The rookie Stephens earned 27 reps. Coach Macdonald obviously believes this strategy was in the Seahawks' best interest.

Haynes did not allow a single QB pressure or sack versus the Commanders, according to Pro Football Focus. He also earned an average-run blocking grade of 63.8 from PFF. Meanwhile, Stephens also wasn't credited with allowing a pressure to Washington's defensive line. Stephens' PFF run-blocking score was 53.4.

Haynes and Stephens will continue competing for reps against the Chargers. It's an interesting strategy. Hopefully it benefits the offensive line.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr.'s back issues got much better after trade to Cowboys, apparently
articles.summary: "When it comes to backs, nobody knows anything, really."
articles.body:
Joey Porter Jr. had been ruled out for Week 4 as a Pittsburgh Steeler . Now that he's a Dallas Cowboy , however, he's feeling much better.

The star cornerback's absence early in the 2026 NFL season was ostensibly for a back injury. It also coincided with the final season of his rookie contract. When an extension that paid him top-of-market cash for a defensive back wasn't in Pittsburgh's plans, Porter Jr. attended practices but didn't participate, creating an unofficial hold-in that technically wasn't about money -- but very obviously was. That bled into the regular season, where the Steelers ruled him out for the first four weeks of the year but did not put him on injured reserve.

Now, after being dealt to the Cowboys and their 32nd-ranked defense, Porter Jr. could be balm in Gilead. He'll also have the opportunity to soothe an oft-burned secondary sooner than expected. Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, there's "a chance" he could join the active roster as soon as Sunday when Dallas travels to face the Houston Texans in an in-state showdown.

The Cowboys need all the help they can get. Offseason addition Cobie Durant missed Week 3's loss to the Baltimore Ravens and hasn't practiced this week. Shavon Revel also did not participate in Wednesday's drills . Fourth round rookie Devin Moore and safety Jalen Thompson are both on injured reserve. That leaves DaRon Bland as the team's top corner -- and he's allowed a passer rating over 100 each of the last two seasons (and through three weeks of this one) following his breakthrough 2023.

Even a diminished Porter Jr. will help. If he plays Sunday against the Texans, we'll have a better idea of just how bad his back really is.

articles.title: John Harbaugh drops brutally honest truth bomb on Giants’ Odell Beckham Jr. release
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr.’s second stint with the New York Giants came to an abrupt end as the team and the veteran wide receiver mutually agreed to part ways. The...
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. 's second stint with the New York Giants came to an abrupt end as the team and the veteran wide receiver mutually agreed to part ways . The decision understandably disappointed many Giants fans, but head coach John Harbaugh offered a candid explanation for why the team ultimately decided it was time to move on.

During an interaction with reporters, Harbaugh openly addressed Beckham's situation and explained that the Giants simply were not getting enough production from the veteran receiver.

"I had a great conversation with Odell, and it was tough, but we just weren't getting enough. It just wasn't working for us. I told him I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted him to be able to do more and get him on the field more," Harbaugh said.

"Whatever reason, we weren't able to do it, put it on us. We weren't able to get it done. But at this point in time, that's kind of where we were, and we needed to move on."

The decision was also influenced by the Giants' roster situation. New York needed to elevate receiver and return specialist Braxton Berrios to the 53-man roster after exhausting its available practice squad elevations.

Before the release, Beckham appeared in all three games for the Giants to begin the 2026 season. However, his opportunities were extremely limited, as he played just 20 offensive snaps and received only one target, which resulted in zero receptions.

OBJ spent the first five seasons of his NFL career with the Giants. His return represented a reunion with the organization that selected him in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft, and he initially secured a spot on the Giants' 53-man roster coming out of training camp.

However, Beckham's NFL future has faced uncertainty on several occasions in recent years. With his second stint in New York now ending after only three games, another chapter of uncertainty begins for the veteran receiver as he looks for his next opportunity .

A finally-poised Bryce Young has made all the difference for the Panthers this year. When he is comfortable, the Panthers move the ball. When he is not, they stall. articles.title: Pack golf teams head to State AA
articles.summary: The Glacier girls golf team was consistent all season — until last week, when it wasn’t. And this was a good thing. Sitting in fifth after the first day of t...
articles.body:
The Glacier girls golf team was consistent all season — until last week, when it wasn't. And this was a good thing.

Sitting in fifth after the first day of the Western AA Divisional, the Wolfpack leap-frogged Flathead on Day 2 for the fourth and final team spot into the State AA tournament, which begins Thursday at Great Falls' Meadowlark Country Club.

First-year Glacier coach Cory Snipes couldn't be more pleased.

"The girls really came through this year," he said. "I don't think they finished better than sixth at any tournament (before divisionals). From my standpoint, that's a huge breakthrough and they had it on a very hard golf course. They played well."

Maggie Mitton, who shot a second-day 82 to take medalist honors, led the way. Lillie Groom was next; her two-day total of 203 left her 12th at the Western AA.

Peyton Cowden, Mari Surdock and Rylee Dutro — the only senior besides Mitton — round out this young team.

Competition will be tougher at state, where Eastern AA champion Billings Senior and Billings West have excellent teams. Senior's Payton Tryan fired a second-day 68 to overtake West standout Paige Loberg for medalist honors, by three strokes.

The Broncs' team total of 668 was nine strokes clear of West and miles ahead of the 753 shot by Western AA champion Missoula Big Sky. The Eagles, led by Charlotte Dale, Zoey Loberg and Jewell Colman, won their divisional by 41 strokes over Sentinel and 45 over Helena Capital.

"Big Sky is going to be a tough one to compete with," Snipes maintained. "Their girls team has been very good all year. If you can keep up with them, you're doing just fine."

Flathead didn't qualify as a team but three Bravettes made state as individuals: Becky Schmidt, Hadley McDonald and Hayden Ward.

"We didn't finish the way we set out to finish, but we've got three girls here at State and they're looking to play their best golf at the end of the season," Flathead coach Phil Jackson said. "That's what it's all about. You try to play consistent and reap the benefits of all their hard work in the offseason."

Flathead had no boys qualify for state while the Glacier squad matched the Pack girls by taking the fourth and final team spot.

The Wolfpack will have to vie once again with the potent boys teams from Helena Capital and Sentinel, along with Eastern AA squads Great Falls CMR, Bozeman and Gallatin. Bozeman and Bozeman both had two-day totals of 594 at their divisional; Jack Prinski of CMR and Bozeman's Will Benne but shot a two-day total of 139.

For Glacier, Tripp O'Boyle (73) had a great second day at the Western AA meet, while Torren Murray placed seventh with a two-day total of 150. Louis Groom, Elliot Anderson and Mac Anderson round out a dangerous squad.

"I do believe the boys can be in those top three spots," said Snipes, whose club had a two-day score of 629. "They have to play consistent and play smart, and realize they're going from one hard course at divisionals (Butte Country Club) to another extremely difficult course."

Capital's boys (597) won the Western AA by 13 strokes with medalist Jayce Belzer, John Gilbert and Matt Gilbert leading the way. Sentinel's Cole Jenkins, Jack Schaefer and Joseph Meusey lead a talented Sentinel squad.

Whatever happens, Snipes has been impressed by his golfers.

"I've loved it," he said. "I've had a great year, and the kids have been awesome to work with. Some ups and downs and some surprises as well. It's been great."

articles.title: Jaguars vs. Bengals: Matchup History Through the Decades
articles.summary: Former AFC Central Division rivals, the Jaguars and Bengals, have played each other 26 times, and the series is currently tied
articles.body:
After a spectacular performance at home against the New England Patriots , the Jacksonville Jaguars are back on the road in Cincinnati this week. The former AFC Central Division rivals have played each other 26 times , and the series is currently tied. Jimmy Smith said the Jags are going to beat the Bengals' asses, so let's look back at the Jaguars doing exactly that on the Bengals' home turf through the decades.

Week 8 on October 31, 1999 Final score: Jaguars 41 – Bengals 10 Attendance: 49,138

I figured an October win would be the best way to start this. During 30:01 of possession, the Jaguars recorded 23 first downs and 377 total net yards. Defensive dominance led to touchdowns from Fred Taylor, Keenan McCardell, Jimmy Smith, and two field goals from Mike Hollis, being the only points scored during the first half. After a Bengals field goal, Jimmy Stewart ran for two touchdowns in the second half. The Bengals scored their first and only touchdown during the fourth quarter. Mark Brunell completed 11 out of 19 attempted passes for 145 yards and was sacked once for a loss of ten yards. Taylor led the team with 128 rushing yards, and Smith led with 89 receiving yards. Aaron Beasley and Donovin Darius both had interceptions. Tony Brackens, Kevin Hardy, Aaron Beasley, Carnell Lake, and Joel Smeenge registered four sacks on Akili Smith for a loss of 21 yards.

Week 15 on December 15, 2002 Final score: Jaguars 29 – Bengals 15 Attendance: 42,092

The numbers were more closely aligned with this one. Jacksonville had 20 first downs, 321 total net yards, and a 30:01 time of possession, compared to Cincinati's 19 first downs, 300 total net yards, and 29:59 time of possession. Kevin Lockett, Pete Mitchell, Jimmy Smith, and Stacey Mack scored touchdowns. Mark Brunell completed 19 out of 28 attempted passes for 223 yards and was sacked three times for a loss of 11 yards. Fred Taylor led the team with 71 rushing yards, and Smith led with 98 receiving yards. Jason Craft picked off Jon Kitna. John Henderson, Marcus Stroud, Paul Spicer, and Marco Coleman recorded three sacks on Kitna for a loss of 23 yards. T.J. Slaughter, Wali Rainer, and Donovin Darius led the team with six combined tackles each.

Week 7 on October 20, 2019 Final score: Jaguars 27 – Bengals 17 Attendance: 42,784

Josh Lambo 's field goals kept the Jags in the game scoring-wise until the fourth quarter, when Gardner Minshew connected with Keelan Cole for a touchdown, and Yannick Ngakoue returned an interception for a 23-yard touchdown, sealing the win for Jacksonville. Lambo contributed 13 of the points scored. Minshew completed 15 out of 32 attempted passes and was sacked twice for a loss of 11 yards. Leonard Fournette led the team with 131 rushing yards, and Dede Westbrook led with 103 passing yards. In addition to Ngakoue's interception, Ronnie Harrison had a 35-yard interception, and Myles Jack had a 14-yard interception. Josh Hines-Allen and Abry Jones sacked Andy Dalton twice for a loss of 18 yards.

I have a good feeling that this is the year.

Please share your favorite memories from the Jaguars vs. Bengals series with us in the comments or on social media. Not following Big Cat Country on social media? It was around a year ago that the podcast "Pablo Torre Finds Out" released the first episode of what would become a 17-part series into alleged efforts by the Los Angeles Clippers to circumvent the NBA's salary cap rules.

Since then, the podcast team has netted a Pulitzer Prize, a National Magazine Award and an Edward R. Murrow Award for its independent investigative reporting on the story.

On Sept. 2, 2026, the NBA released the findings of its own investigation into the scheme , concluding that the Clippers had helped star forward Kawhi Leonard secure endorsement deals with four companies that did business with the team – and had offered those companies business in return – in violation of the league's salary cap rules.

The punishment amounted to one of the largest in American sports history and included the Clippers being fined US$30 million and stripped of five future first-round draft picks, with team owner Steve Ballmer receiving a one-year suspension.

Yet as "Pablo Torre Finds Out" began unwinding the Clippers' efforts to circumvent the salary cap, legacy sports media outlets largely stood by and watched – when they didn't outright dismiss the podcast's work.

To me, this is a story that showcases the growing importance of independent journalism . But it's also a story about the shortcomings of traditional sports media. As someone who studies how sports is becoming increasingly intertwined with political and corporate power, I can't help but wonder if the sports media is up to the task.

In the heyday of newspapers, the sports page helped sell subscriptions. But it was often disparaged as the " toy department ," since it featured less "hard" or serious reporting.

The sports page's bread and butter has long been game stories, injury reports, trade rumors and opinion columns. Sports radio perfected play-by-play commentary and talk shows that often involved debates with fans. Magazines ran in-depth profiles of individual players and long-form stories about epic playoff battles. Television centered on live game broadcasts, postgame highlights and weekly shows. Books went deeper, whether through biographies about the lives of coaches and athletes or narratives of memorable seasons that detailed the construction of championship squads .

Over the years, these formats coexisted to create a relatively balanced media diet. At times, they were even able to produce noteworthy investigative stories: Boston College basketball's point-shaving scandal in the 1980s; the pervasiveness of performance-enhancing drug use in MLB during the 1990s and 2000s; and what the NFL knew about long-term brain damage linked to repeated head injuries in the 2010s.

But because the intermingling of sports with politics and finance now runs so deep, holding power to account often requires investigations that transcend regular sports reporting. The Athletic's Adam Crafton, for example, spent months digging through host-city contracts and public records in order to show how FIFA had shifted World Cup costs onto U.S. taxpayers .

Yet Crafton's reporting and research for The Athletic remains an exception; much of the watchdog journalism on the sports industry has to be taken up by outlets that aren't sports-centric, yet have an investigative reporting infrastructure already in place.

For example, ProPublica was able to expose the tax-evasion practices of wealthy sports teams owners in 2021. And in April 2026, Wired revealed how Madison Square Garden, the home of the New York Knicks and New York Rangers, was secretly using facial recognition technology to identify people entering its venues and compile profiles of them.

The changing media landscape in the digital age has created openings for podcasters like Torre. But it has also made it more difficult to distinguish journalistic rigor from public relations.

Fans can now get their sports news from a motley crew of formats and personalities , ranging from social media personalities and podcasters to YouTube channels and streamers.

Meanwhile, the line between sports leagues and the media outlets that cover them has blurred. In January 2026, ESPN bought the NFL's official TV network . Almost all major franchises now feature in-house media teams that run their own stories and social media accounts to compete with traditional outlets. The owner of the Boston Red Sox , John W. Henry, also happens to own the New England Sports Network and Boston's primary newspaper of record , the Boston Globe.

Athlete-owned media channels like PlayersTV might offer an interesting window into athletes' lives and perspectives, but these formats will always have strong incentives to veer into self-promotion.

The fragmentation of traditional sports media has occurred alongside the growing financialization of sports.

By financialization of sports, I mean the ways in which sports teams, leagues and athletes are increasingly seen as financial assets and vehicles for investment, rather than cultural or sporting institutions.

Because U.S. professional sports leagues operate as tightly controlled, closed markets , they can determine who is allowed into teams and what size stakes they can hold. Private equity was only recently granted permission to start investing in pro sports leagues. But even then, across the five major North American leagues, private equity firms' involvement has been capped at a maximum of 30% of noncontrolling ownership.

That hasn't made investment any less attractive, as sports teams have tended to regularly outperform the stock market by several degrees of magnitude.

Take the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers. In August 2026, Mark Walter sold the team for $12.5 billion, a record-breaking sum in the history of professional sports. The sale took place less than a year after he bought a controlling interest in the team for a then-record valuation of approximately $10 billion, meaning the team's valuation had increased 25% in just nine months.

Going back even further, Jerry Jones bought the NFL's Dallas Cowboys for $150 million in 1989; as of September 2026 , the franchise is worth $17 billion – an inflation-adjusted return of roughly 4,155%.

For these reasons, institutional investors such as RedBird Capital Partners and Arctos Partners have entered the sports market in recent years. On Aug. 11, 2026, MLB's New York Yankees announced a $2.6 billion financing deal with Apollo Global Management that includes an eventual 16% stake in the team and values the Yankees at more than $12 billion.

Bloomberg reports on Apollo Global Management's $2.6 billion deal with the New York Yankees – and what it means for future sports financing.

It's easy to see why investors are drawn to professional sports.

Live sports remain one of the few areas of American life with genuine mass appeal that transcends politics, race and class. Virtually all top broadcasts and most-watched shows every year are sporting events.

Beyond a financial return, wealthy investors and entities see valuable teams and leagues as a way to purchase credibility in the eyes of the public through what's called " sportswashing ," or using the widespread popularity of sports to burnish their reputations .

But the new streams of capital have created opportunities for financial misconduct. The Miami-based investment firm 777 Partners built a portfolio of international soccer clubs as part of an ambitious expansion financed by its broader investment business. The firm unraveled in 2025 after prosecutors accused its founder and chief financial officer of concealing hundreds of millions of dollars in financial problems from lenders and investors, a case bolstered by the CFO's guilty plea .

Meanwhile, the rise of sports betting, fantasy leagues and prediction markets has further turned sports into a vehicle for financial speculation . And billions of taxpayer dollars continue to subsidize massive stadium projects, despite limited economic benefits and weak public support .

I think the unlikely success of an independent reporter like Pablo Torre can serve as a teachable moment for sports journalism.

In a forthcoming article for the International Journal of Sport Communication , sports media scholar Roxane Coche and I argue how sports journalists could embrace more of a watchdog, investigative role in their coverage.

We suggest that sports journalists could have basic economics training to put them in a better position to report on financial schemes, analyze U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filings or understand cryptocurrencies. And then there are basic watchdog journalism methods that could be integrated into their everyday reporting: surveying public records, mining documents and fact-checking statements.

Sports has never simply been about which team wins and which team loses on a given day. But it's becoming impossible to ignore the ways in which politics, finance, fanbases and athletes are increasingly reshaping the sports landscape.

In just the past 12 months, Josh Kushner, whose brother is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, bought a stake in the Los Angeles Lakers . NBA and MLB players have been caught up in gambling investigations , and FIFA has explored selling a stake in its commercial rights to private investors.

These are all sports stories that warrant closer scrutiny.

Alex Volonte does not work for, consult, own shares in or receive funding from any company or organization that would benefit from this article, and has disclosed no relevant affiliations beyond their academic appointment.

articles.title: Drake Maye Gets Unexpected Defense As Rob Gronkowski Blames Patriots’ Offense For Ugly Start
articles.summary: Drake Maye came into this season with expectations that few young quarterbacks have to handle. He was coming off a Super Bowl appearance, finished second in...
articles.body:
Drake Maye came into this season with expectations that few young quarterbacks have to handle. He was coming off a Super Bowl appearance, finished second in the MVP voting and had already shown New England that he could carry a big part of its offense.

Three weeks later, Maye's confidence appears to have dropped. The Patriots are 1-2, while Maye has thrown six interceptions and scored only one touchdown. New England is averaging 12 points per game, showing how badly the offense has struggled. Those results have brought more attention and pressure on Maye whenever the Patriots fail to score.

Rob Gronkowski Sees Something Different With Drake Maye

That is where Rob Gronkowski offered a different view of what is happening. Speaking on Up & Adams , the former Patriots star argued that the problem is much bigger than Maye simply playing poorly.

"They do need A.J. Brown back," Gronkowski said. "There is literally no one open on the field."

Gronkowski believes New England's receivers are making Maye's job harder by failing to get open. Instead of making clear, simple throws, Maye often has to pass into tight coverage.

"He's gonna have to stick it in every single time into a tight window," Gronkowski said. His comment shows how little room Maye has to make mistakes.

Gronkowski did not clear Maye of responsibility for the offense's problems. He said the quarterback must become more confident, but he also stressed that the entire offense must improve.

A.J. Brown's Absence Has Exposed The Bigger Issue

A.J. Brown joined New England from Philadelphia to give the offense another proven outside receiver. He caught four passes for 51 yards and a touchdown in the opener before a high ankle sprain sent him to injured reserve.

New England's offense has struggled without Brown. His absence has left Maye with one fewer reliable target in the passing game.

Maye completed 14 of 25 passes for 199 yards against Jacksonville . He also threw two interceptions and lost a fumble before being removed late in the 35-6 loss.

The Patriots scored only six points in that game. Their poor performance showed that the offense has problems beyond one player or one position.

The turnovers remain a major concern. Six interceptions in three games have repeatedly ended drives and given opponents more chances with the ball.

Gronkowski pointed to another problem that does not always appear in the main statistics. New England's receivers have struggled to get open, leaving Maye with fewer safe passing options.

That makes Maye's job harder when a play breaks down. It also gives him less room to make a mistake when he must hold the ball or force a difficult throw.

"There's only so much you can do as an offensive coordinator," Gronkowski said, pointing to the talent and the lack of receivers getting open consistently.

Brown's return could help with more than his own catches. He would give Maye another proven target and force defenses to cover more of the field.

Brown can return in Week 6. By then, the Patriots may have a better idea of whether Maye is the main problem or just one part of a struggling offense.

articles.title: Lazio Could Anticipate New Transfer Ban by Signing Former Everton Stalwart
articles.summary: With the risk of a January ban becoming increasingly concrete, Lazio might decide to add another player to their ranks while they still can, reportedly setti...
articles.body:
With the risk of a January ban becoming increasingly concrete, Lazio might decide to add another player to their ranks while they still can, reportedly setting their sights on Abdoulaye Doucoure .

Why Lazio Are Bracing Themselves for Another Transfer Ban

The Biancocelesti will be expected to hand their half-yearly financial report to the commission that oversees the accounts of the Serie A clubs before November 30. This report will cover the period from April 1 to September 30. The commission will study Lazio's numbers and decide whether to give them the license to operate on the market in January.

(Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

At this stage, most sources believe the Italian capital club won't be able to meet the required labour cost threshold of 0.7, as they're expected to register circa 0.82. This figure certainly won't be enough for Lazio to operate freely on the market, so they risk a transfer ban, similar to the summer of 2025, or at least a net-zero restriction, like the summer of 2026.

Why Lazio Are in a Rush to Sign Free Agents

According to La Lazio Siamo Noi , the management could thus seize the opportunity to bolster their squad while they still can. Since the transfer market is currently closed, Lazio can only sign players on free transfers, so Angelo Fabiani and company continue to track free agents. It should be noted that the club left a vacant spot on the Serie A squad list after omitting Luca Pellegrini .

The source adds that Lazio are studying a move for Doucoure, a box-to-box midfielder renowned for his time in England. The 33-year-old is a youth product of Stade Rennais who moved to Watford in 2016. After four years with the Londoners, he joined Everton in 2020 and went on to cement himself as a fan favourite at Goodison Park.

Abdoulaye Doucoure (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

In the summer of 2025, the Malian signed for Saudi Pro League club NEOM, but he ended his experience after a solitary year, so he's been unattached since July.

articles.summary: Sean Everitt has challenged his Edinburgh players to maintain the momentum built from an excellent opening victory away to Ulster in the URC when they face t...
articles.body:
Sean Everitt has challenged his Edinburgh players to maintain the momentum built from an excellent opening victory away to Ulster in the URC when they face the Stormers at Hive Stadium on Friday night.

A stunning performance in the first 55 minutes helped Edinburgh run in four tries as they raced into a 34-5 lead, and while they were left holding on as Ulster came roaring back, the capital side left Belfast with the maximum five points.

After a disappointing 12th-place finish in the URC last season, Everitt now wants his side to get points on the league table early this time around.

"It's extremely important," said the head coach. "We didn't start well last year and we were on the back foot immediately.

"We've got the five points now and building momentum is key. Hopefully the youngsters that played last week can take a lot of experience out of that game away from home.

"It's exciting for them to play in front of our fans at Hive Stadium on a Friday night. So yes, it's really important to continue with the momentum, especially with an away game [against Zebre] coming up and then a European game [at home to Toulon] thereafter."

Pierre Schoeman returns to the side having been rested for the Ulster match, with Ollie Blyth-Lafferty also coming into the front row.

The rest of the pack remains unchanged, as does the backline that attacked so impressively in Belfast.

Edinburgh team to face Stormers: Piers O'Conor, Malelili Satala, Matt Currie (co-capt), Kienan Higgins, Geordie Gwynn, James Grayson, Hector Patterson; Pierre Schoeman, Harri Morris, Ollie Blyth-Lafferty, Callum Hunter-Hill, Glen Young, Liam McConnell, Freddy Douglas, Magnus Bradbury (co-capt).

Replacements: Jerry Blyth-Lafferty, Alec Hepburn, Paul Hill, Euan McVie, Tom Currie, Conor McAlpine, Cammy Scott, Rory McHaffie.

articles.title: 5 Cornerbacks Lions Could Target After Joey Porter Jr. Trade
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions missed out on Joey Porter Jr., but five potential cornerback trade targets could give Brad Holmes another opportunity to upgrade the second...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions took their shot at Joey Porter Jr., but the former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback is headed somewhere else. That doesn't necessarily mean Brad Holmes is finished looking for help in Detroit's secondary.

Dallas acquired Porter from Pittsburgh for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection after multiple teams showed interest. The Lions had explored a potential deal for Porter , giving us a significant clue about how Holmes views his current cornerback situation.

Detroit's interest matters because this wasn't simply outside speculation connecting a talented player to a contender. Holmes was willing to investigate adding another starting-caliber cornerback, and missing on Porter doesn't eliminate the reasons Detroit made that call in the first place.

The Lions can now turn elsewhere if Holmes remains interested in upgrading the position. There are several very different paths he could take depending on whether Detroit wants a long-term starter, a veteran rental or a low-cost gamble.

Mike Payton Identifies Five Potential Lions Targets

Mike Payton of A to Z Sports identified five cornerbacks who could make sense for Detroit following the Porter trade. His list includes Zyon McCollum , Riley Moss , Donte Jackson , Marlon Humphrey and Cam Taylor-Britt .

It's an intriguing collection because those five players would represent dramatically different types of acquisitions. McCollum and Moss could potentially become pieces beyond 2026, Jackson offers veteran experience, Humphrey would represent an aggressive win-now move, and Taylor-Britt could be the inexpensive change-of-scenery gamble.

There is an important distinction to make before going any further. None of these five players has been reported as an active Lions trade target, so they should be viewed as potential fits rather than players Holmes is known to be pursuing.

Still, Detroit's interest in Porter changes the conversation surrounding potential cornerback trades. Holmes has already demonstrated that he is at least willing to explore options outside the organization.

Zyon McCollum Would Be Much More Than a Rental

If Detroit wants another young outside corner rather than a temporary fix, Zyon McCollum is one of the most interesting possibilities. The 27-year-old Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback stands 6-foot-2 and has developed into an established NFL starter.

McCollum would also require considerably more commitment than a typical in-season acquisition. He signed a three-year, $48 million extension with Tampa Bay , so acquiring him would mean bringing a significant contract onto Detroit's books beyond the current season.

That long-term commitment is also part of the appeal. Instead of spending draft capital on a player who could leave after the season, Detroit could potentially pair McCollum with D.J. Reed and create some stability on the outside.

Holmes would have to decide whether that stability is worth the financial investment and whatever Tampa Bay would demand in return. This wouldn't be a simple October rental designed to survive a few months.

Riley Moss Could Give Lions Another Young Building Block

Riley Moss represents another potential path toward a younger solution. The 26-year-old Denver Broncos cornerback is in the final season of his rookie contract and already has substantial starting experience.

Denver's depth at cornerback makes Moss an interesting player to watch, although there is no indication the Broncos are actively trying to move him. Patrick Surtain II anchors the secondary, while Ja'Quan McMillian and 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron give Denver additional talent at the position.

The challenge for Detroit would be convincing a competitive Broncos team to surrender a useful defensive back. Teams with postseason expectations generally don't trade players who can help them win unless the return makes the decision worthwhile.

Moss would nevertheless fit Detroit's competitive timeline. The Lions could add a cornerback still entering his prime and then decide after the season whether he deserves a longer commitment.

Donte Jackson Would Be the Straightforward Rental

If Holmes prefers a shorter-term solution, Donte Jackson becomes considerably more interesting. The veteran cornerback brings extensive starting experience without requiring Detroit to commit significant future money beyond this season.

Jackson is 31, so nobody would mistake this for a long-term solution to Detroit's cornerback situation. The attraction would be adding an experienced defender for a team attempting to make another deep postseason run.

Sometimes that is exactly what a contender needs at the trade deadline. Detroit doesn't necessarily have to identify its starting cornerbacks for the next four seasons before improving the 2026 roster.

The Lions also have reason to continue evaluating what they already have in the building. Ennis Rakestraw Jr. earned additional opportunities from Dan Campbell after an encouraging performance against the Jets , and his development could influence how aggressively Detroit pursues outside help.

Adding a veteran wouldn't necessarily block Rakestraw's opportunity, either. Detroit can continue developing its former second-round pick while strengthening the overall depth of a secondary that will inevitably deal with injuries and difficult matchups over a 17-game season.

Marlon Humphrey Would Be the All-In Move

Then there is Marlon Humphrey , who would represent a completely different level of acquisition. If Jackson is the practical veteran option, Humphrey would be the aggressive swing for a team convinced it can win right now.

Humphrey has spent his entire career with Baltimore and brings a résumé that none of the other four players on this list can match. He has earned multiple Pro Bowl selections and possesses the versatility to play outside or move around the secondary depending on the matchup.

The financial component would make any potential deal complicated. Humphrey carries a significant contract, and Baltimore would have its own cap considerations before even deciding whether moving one of its most recognizable defenders makes football sense.

Detroit would therefore need several things to align before a Humphrey trade became realistic. The Ravens would have to be willing to listen, the compensation would have to fit Holmes' valuation, and Detroit would need to be comfortable absorbing the financial commitment.

The appeal is easy to understand despite those obstacles. Humphrey is the type of established veteran a contender acquires because it believes one additional impact defender could matter in January.

Cam Taylor-Britt Could Be the Low-Cost Wild Card

Cam Taylor-Britt might be the most intriguing gamble of the five because his current value is difficult to determine. The former Cincinnati Bengals starter is now with Indianapolis and hasn't occupied the same prominent defensive role he once held.

Taylor-Britt started 40 games during four seasons with Cincinnati, so there is a meaningful NFL résumé beneath his current situation. Detroit also has familiarity with him from the pre-draft process after hosting him before the Bengals selected him in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft.

That history doesn't mean Holmes is interested now, but it does remove some of the mystery surrounding the player. Detroit's scouting department already did extensive work on Taylor-Britt before he entered the league.

A change of scenery could make sense if Indianapolis doesn't view him as a significant part of its defense. For Detroit, the attraction would be betting on a talented player whose value may currently be lower than it was earlier in his career.

Those are the kinds of transactions that can pay off without requiring a contender to sacrifice premium draft capital. Holmes has never been afraid to trust his evaluations when another organization views a player differently.

Joey Porter Jr. Trade Should Keep Brad Holmes Calling

Missing on Porter doesn't mean the Lions should suddenly panic and trade for the first cornerback who becomes available. It does, however, reveal that Holmes was willing to investigate making a meaningful addition to his secondary.

That matters because Detroit's original reasons for calling Pittsburgh didn't disappear when Dallas completed the trade. Porter simply became unavailable, forcing the Lions to decide whether there is another player worth pursuing at the right price.

McCollum and Moss would represent potential investments beyond this season. Jackson and Humphrey offer different levels of veteran experience, while Taylor-Britt presents the kind of lower-cost gamble that could produce significant value if Detroit believes it can unlock him.

The financial component will also matter, especially with several Lions eventually requiring new contracts of their own. A look at the NFL's current cornerback contracts shows how dramatically the commitment can change depending on whether Holmes targets a younger established starter or a short-term veteran.

Maybe one of these five players ends up wearing Honolulu blue before the trade deadline. Maybe Holmes has another name on his board that hasn't surfaced publicly at all.

What we know is that the Lions were interested enough in Porter to make the call. Now that Porter is a Cowboy, Holmes has to decide whether there is another cornerback worth calling about.

articles.title: 3 Things That Worry Me About Vanderbilt
articles.summary: Upstart crowing they stole our QB, Homecoming, Aaron Murray on the TV call, and a tropical storm. What… me worry?
articles.body:
First, here's why I'm NOT worried about the fightin' Powder Monkeys:

1. The 3 rd in the country ranked Bulldog rushing defense will not face much of a test again this week, I'm afraid. Vanderbilt is 106 th running the ball, only averaging 132 yards a game on the ground.

Now they are certainly trying to run it. Only once, in a comeback effort against NC State where they had to throw the ball, have the Commodores attempted less than 38 rushes. If the current trend continues, and that trend being UGA outscoring opponents 63-0 in the first quarter and 133-12 in the first half, then Glen Schumann can probably tell the boys to pin their ears back and go after Jared Curtis en masse.

2. Speaking of Jordan Rodgers 2.0, the Vanderbilt QB may be all that, but he's still a freshman. Did he lead a comeback against NC State? Yes. Jared Curtis drove the 'Dores down the field late in the fourth, and threw a beautiful touchdown to get within 3 with just a few minutes left on the clock. He also threw an ill-advised, trying to do too much, what should have been a game-ending interception into double coverage with just a minute or so left. If it wasn't for NC State s***, that pick would be what everyone remembers.

And another reason why Georgia might start bringing some pressure to see if Curtis can make more freshman mistakes.

3. Was Georgia lucky that adding Texas and Oklahoma in the 2024 season eliminated SEC divisions and took a Miley Cyrus wrecking ball to the schedule so that we didn't have to face Vanderbilt? Very possibly yes. Yet even the loyal Commodore fanbase is starting to conclude that Head Coach Lea Clark caught lightning in a bottle when he hired Jerry Kill from New Mexico State, and Diego Pavia is officially out of temporary restraining orders. Add to that Kirby is 52-0 against unranked opponents. This is a not the plucky underdog darling Vanderbilt of 2024-2025

Now forgive me, as I was weaned at the nipple of Larry Munson's scratch so here's what does worry me about seeing a Vandy team that thinks it belongs in the post-season:

1 . Should we talk about the weather? I'm no meteorologist, but I've heard tell there's wet weather heading to the Athens area Saturday. And that is probably the best thing Vanderbilt Coach Clark Lea can bring to Sanford Stadium.

Wet weather will definitely slow down explosiveness and hamper any tempo from the Georgia offense. Wet balls affect both throwing and catching, and Vandy would prefer nothing better than to bog this game down in the mud, keeping the scores low and close, and hoping for more good fortune or a horrible Bulldog mistake. Recent guidance is saying the rain may not arrive until late afternoon, so an early kick might actually work in our favor and allow the Georgia advantages to bear fruit on the field.

2. So Hold On. Half of the 14 possessions vs. Oklahoma – 5 punts, 1 fumble, and 1 interception – ended without points and with giving the ball back to the bad guys. Plus Georgia was only 3 of 12 on 3 rd down (there was a successful 4 th down conversion in there).

And this is an area where the Vanderbilt is pretty good. They successfully defended 90% of 3 rd downs in their first game, 80% in the 2 nd , and more than 50% in the last two games against Power4 competition. That is allowing opponents to convert 3 rd downs less than a third of the time… not too shabby with a third of the season complete.

They also have not 1, but 2 players with punt return touchdowns this season. Even more reason to keep the ball, and only give it to Vanderbilt when kicking off from the 35 yard line.

3 . Coming in a hurry with the furies, breathing down. Your. Neck. Georgia's sack numbers are vastly improved over last season, and the lads are definitely getting in the backfield on the reg. Tackles for loss are up too, 26 this season vs. 18 in 2025 through 4 games. But just because you're penetrating doesn't mean you bring the ball carrier down.

Too many times did I see John Mateer face pressure, only to slip out and move forward. He's elusive, but Jared Curtis is a good athlete too. It reminds me of the Ole Miss CFP game – getting a red helmet or two pursuing the QB only to see overpursuit, and not keeping any lane discipline, then watching a pass downfield or a positive gain on the ground. Our guys can push up front, but they also need to contain. And this can burn us this weekend, as well as against the elite athletes we're about to face the next few weeks.

Call me crazy, just don't call me late fordinner. Let us know in the comments what you're feeling about hosting the Vanderbilt Commodores and Clark Lea's butter balm delivery van. And as always…
